authoring.cwd_rule: runSkill and sendToSession launch the user's agent CLI in a DIFFERENT working directory than the doc — pass ABSOLUTE paths, never doc-relative ones. Build them from getDocDir() (the board's own dir, available without an open epic); getEpicHandle() also yields an absolute anchor but only inside an open epic. readWorkspace is the exception: it is confined to the doc's OWN directory subtree, so it takes './'-relative paths.
authoring.examples: The CodeSense docs context repo (org codesense/docs, bundled with every install and listed in the context repo menu) has working reference dashboards in its getting-started team under content/examples/dashboards/ — kickoff-console.html (query + taxonomy + act('openWorkspace') + act('setStatus', {path, status})), sprint-analysis.html (query + sprints + taxonomy), agent-inbox-console.html (sessions + roles + inbox + act('replyAsHuman') / act('markRead'), live on onAgentsChanged / onInboxChanged), with routine snapshots for external data. Copy one into your team's or Private content to start from it, and validate the finished dashboard before use.

get_doc_dir.returns: the ABSOLUTE directory of this dashboard doc; null when no dashboard is mounted.
get_doc_dir.use: The anchor for building an absolute path to a SIBLING doc (e.g. a story) for runSkill — available WITHOUT an open epic workspace. `abs = getDocDir() + '/' + name`.

get_epic_handle.returns: the epic's ABSOLUTE doc path (epicDocPath) when this dashboard is hosted INSIDE an open epic workspace; otherwise null.
get_epic_handle.use: How a dashboard addresses the epic's already-running agent (the `target` for sendToSession). When null, the doc is not inside an OPEN epic workspace — HIDE the epic-chat controls, never render a dead button. (For sibling absolute paths, prefer getDocDir, which needs no open epic.)

authoring.non_blocking: Never await a full readWorkspace sweep before first paint. Paint the shell + skeleton rows synchronously, THEN hydrate rows off the read promises (Promise.all) so the UI is interactive immediately.
authoring.role: Everything a dashboard AUTHOR needs to build an acting dashboard WITHOUT reading the CodeSense source — the doc scaffold, the epic-addressing primitive, the working-directory rule, and the pre-ship check.
authoring.scaffold: Add `<meta name="cs:type" content="dashboard">` to <head> so the doc is enumerable as a dashboard. Nothing else needs declaring: call any verb directly.
authoring.validate: Run validate_live_data_doc on your HTML before shipping: it flags a setStatus call addressed by storyId instead of path (blocking), a sendToSession target not resolved via getEpicHandle (advisory), and unsafe innerHTML (advisory).

action.call: await window.codesense.act(verb, args) → Promise. `act` is a thin convenience wrapper over the same invoke RPC. Resolves with the verb's result; REJECTS with a typed-prefix Error when the call fails.
action.enforcement: The runaway guards, the concurrency cap and managed-path confinement run in the CodeSense process, NEVER in your doc's JS. Your act() call is convenience; those guards live behind it.
action.errors: A failed call REJECTS the act() Promise with a STABLE typed prefix — branch on `err.message.startsWith(...)`: `denied: write budget` (metadata runaway guard) · `denied: route not applied (…)` · `denied: send budget` (chat rate) · `denied: prefs budget` (setPrefs burst) · `denied: spawn budget` (cap-free open burst) · `busy` (concurrency cap saturated) · `not-allowed:` (runSkill: a prompt-splitting skill name / control-char arg) · `unavailable:` (backend / workspace context / agent CLI down) · `traversal:` / `unsupported-type:` / `too-large:` / `binary:` / `not-found:` (readWorkspace path/content rejects) · `refused:` / `not-found:` (openFile outside a known team content root, or a missing file) · `invalid:` (setField: a bad key name or value) · a verbatim CodeSense reject for an out-of-bounds (non-managed) path. Same typed-prefix convention as `analyze`.

policy.effectiveGrant: The Rust frame record holds policyGrant intersected with principalScopes. Open grants the full vocabulary by default; team-safe intersects declarations with slot and scope ceilings. Per-dashboard grant overrides replace the policy grant. Missing capabilities reject with denied: grant before confirmation or budgets. Inbox projection calls resolve inbox:read:team or inbox:read:all-teams from the stored frame view. Records calls resolve own or team reach from the collection in the stored frame binding; records subscriptions require its read capability.
policy.host: Confirmations survive frame unmount, suspend every frame, focus Cancel and ignore Confirm for 500 ms. Private and built-in prompt-once callers may choose Always. Team and message callers only allow once. Cancellation consumes the budget.

mcpApps.result: CallToolResult: content, structuredContent, isError; a pending call resolves after the host answer.

policy.precedence: Per-dashboard confirmation overrides win over preset and switches. Team-safe message grants are checked before any confirmation policy.

confirmMessageDestructive.description: Confirm destructive and send verbs from HTML messages; team-safe denies them before any dialog.

confirmTeamSendAsYou.description: Confirm sends as you from team dashboards. Never offers Always.

privateInstall.description: Copy team dashboards with private reach into the private space. Enabled by team-safe.

action.role: Beyond READING data, any HTML doc in your spaces can ACT — mutate CodeSense state through the bridge verbs (flip a story's status, route a file into context, draft a doc, open a workspace, run a skill, chat to a running agent). With the default open policy, every allowlisted verb runs when called without a prompt. Opt-in policy can require a host confirmation.
action.safe_output: Treat any value an action returns — and all upstream/model data — as unsafe input: render with textContent / createElement, never innerHTML / outerHTML / document.write.

tiers.manage: Closes a session the board opened (closeWorkspace) — AUDITED, but NOT budgeted by the metadata write guard and NOT rate-limited like a chat send, so an autonomous cleanup pass can close many finished sessions in a row.
tiers.metadata: Silent frontmatter/file and inbox-state writes (setStatus/setField/routeToContext/draft, markRead/markUnread/archive/setHumanStatus). A runaway guard caps a burst of write calls (a batch `setStatus` is one call); past it the call rejects `denied: write budget` until the burst window passes.
tiers.prefs: Dashboard-local preferences: separate 30 calls per 10 s budget, no audit line.
tiers.read: Reads a file / lists a dir CONFINED to the doc's own directory subtree (readWorkspace), or observes a workspace — AUDITED (read:true), never budgeted.
tiers.send: Injects a chat turn into an already-running agent (sendToSession/sendToWorkspaceTab, and runPrompt), or sends an inbox message (postMessage, sendAsHuman, replyAsHuman) — rate-limited (anti-flood; `denied: send budget`).
tiers.spawn: Opens a workspace / drives an agent (openWorkspace/runPrompt/runSkill/openTab), or opens a file in the viewer (openFile) — bounded by a concurrency cap (`busy` when saturated). Opens that take no cap slot (openFile, openTab, a headed dir/epic openWorkspace) are bounded by a runaway guard instead: past a burst the call rejects `denied: spawn budget` until the window passes.

archive.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. Archive and mark read human-directed messages in the page team in one transaction and at most one inbox change event. Resolves `{archived: n}`, counting newly archived rows once; agent mail, already archived and unknown ids are unchanged. Requires a non-empty array of positive safe integer ids. Store failures reject verbatim so a page can roll back optimistic state.

closeTerminalTab.purpose: Close ONE terminal tab opened via `openWorkspace`/`openTab` (or minted by `open_terminal_tab`/`open_remote_tab` MCP), the symmetric counterpart of the open verbs. `handle` is the opaque tab handle a `sessions()` row carries (a raw sessionId is refused with `unknownHandle`). Terminates the CLI if one is running, closes the tab, drops it from `sessions()`. Works for local AND remote tabs — the handle resolves to its host transparently. Idempotent: a handle whose session already exited returns `{closed: true, alreadyClosed: true}`; a handle nothing ever had returns `{closed: false, reason: "unknownHandle"}`. A session trying to close its OWN tab mid-call is refused with `{closed: false, reason: "selfClose"}` — the reply would never reach it. Does NOT remove the worktree even when closing the last tab (that is `closeWorkspace`'s destructive opt-in — one verb per concept). Rate-guarded.

closeWorkspace.purpose: The CLOSE half of a board-owned session lifecycle, with an optional DESTRUCTIVE escalation. Base behavior: close a session the board opened, addressed by the SAME opaque handle it opened/sends with (a storyId, a `{repo}#{branch}`, or an epicDocPath). Kills the handle-bound session (freeing the concurrency cap + writing one Kill audit line) AND evicts its terminal tab. Resolved CodeSense-side, so a raw session id from the doc can never close another session. Idempotent: a handle with no live binding (already closed / never opened) is a typed no-op, NOT an error — a board can call it defensively. The DEFAULT closes the SESSION, not the worktree — the worktree persists for the next open. The typical loop: `openWorkspace → (runPrompt/sendToSession) → poll getWorkspaceStatus until !live → closeWorkspace`. A still-live target is stopped mid-turn. **DESTRUCTIVE opt-in**: pass `removeWorktree: true` to ALSO reap the managed worktree (git worktree remove + registry prune) — the symmetric close of an `openWorkspace({storyId})`. DIRTY-GUARDED: a worktree with uncommitted tracked/untracked edits or unpushed commits is refused with `{closed: false, reason: "dirty", dirty: {uncommittedFiles, unpushedCommits}}` and nothing is removed. ESCALATION: pass `discardUnsaved: true` on TOP of `removeWorktree: true` to force the removal over that dirty state; the response lists what was lost in `discardedUnsavedWork`. CodeSense-managed hydrated files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, …) are always excluded from the dirty check (AC-8). A team-workspace close with `removeWorktree: true` returns `{worktreeRemoved: false, reason: "noManagedWorktree"}` — the content root is NEVER removed. A remote-machine workspace returns `{worktreeRemoved: false, reason: "remoteWorktreeReapDeferred"}` — removing the worktree directory on a remote machine is not supported yet. Rate-guarded like every other `codesense.act(...)` surface.

commands.run.purpose: Run a slot dashboard's declared command by its `<dashboard>/<command>` id from `commands.list()`, as the person's chord or the command palette does: the host reveals the dashboard's slot when needed and delivers `codesense:command` once, after that page's `ready()`. The page acts for the person, so a humans-only command runs. Needs `commands:run` in the calling frame's grant (open grants it). The MCP twin `command_run` is the agent's: it is refused for humans-only commands and for dashboards whose grant lacks `commands:run`. Resolves `{requested: true}`; `unavailable:` for an inactive command.

dismiss_agent_mark.purpose: Acknowledge the session's current crash mark. Any caller who can read the session may dismiss it, without confirmation. Uses the same persistent Rust write as native and MCP; a new crash has a new identity.

draft.purpose: Create + seed a NEW managed content doc derived from `from` at tier `level`.

embedMessage.args: {messageId: number, org?: string, team?: string, release?: boolean, frameId?: string}
embedMessage.purpose: Embed an inbox HTML message inline in a right-pane dashboard. The host mints an isolated message frame and returns {url, frameId, height, allow}. Architecture: set iframe.allow to the returned allow value before assigning src, so the host-drawn Copy action can write the clipboard from the child. This is browser delegation, not a new app grant. Human-authored HTML returns {html} through the existing sanitizer. Agent-addressed mail is refused. Pass release:true and the returned frameId when removing an embedded message. The URL contains no token; a live child talks directly to the host with its own identity and stored message team. Explicit team targets use the same inbox grant checks as openMessage.

files.create.purpose: Create a content file with fail or keep-both collision behavior; returns {path}. MCP twin: create_content_file.

files.delete.purpose: Delete a content file; returns {deletedPath}. MCP twin: delete_content_file.

files.list.purpose: List own team, private, story hydration or agent context files; returns {rows}. MCP twin: list_context_content.

files.move.purpose: Move a content file; returns {fromPath, toPath}. MCP twin: move_content_file.

files.read.purpose: Read a content file; returns {text?, bytesUrl?, size, truncated, sha256}. MCP twin: read_content_file.

getWorkspaceStatus.purpose: The OBSERVE half of a dir/story dashboard: return `{exists, live, sessionId}` for a story's workspace, so a board renders the HONEST affordance — `exists:false` → Launch, `exists:true` → Focus, `live:true` → running — for a story it did NOT itself open. Open-state is the launch-source-agnostic viewer open list (a story worktree opened in the normal CodeSense viewer is observed too — the whole point), and `live` is a REAL child `try_wait` probe (never map membership, never 'a tab exists'). Poll it to stay current as the session starts/ends. A read: AUDITED (read:true, the observed storyId), never budgeted.

gotoAgent.purpose: Show an agent by handle or bare definition id through the native Show path: select and reveal its tab (restoring or adopting it if needed), switch its team, open saved output, or state why it cannot be shown. With preserveFocus:true the tab is still activated but keyboard focus stays on the calling frame. Without it the terminal takes focus as usual. Resolves {located,outcome}.

launchUnder.purpose: Open the native launch sheet under a running agent, prefilled with its placement team, manager handle and story; task optionally fills the initial task. The person still clicks Launch in the sheet. Unknown handle rejects with unavailable: no such agent. Presentation only; agents launch with open_workspace.

loadMedia.deny_example: media is off in team config
loadMedia.purpose: Load an inbox image from the Inbox pane after the person taps and confirms in the host. Message frames are refused. Requires inbox:write; pass both org and team for a synced team, otherwise use the page team. Fetches pending or retryable failed media through the host and emits the normal inbox change. Refuses when the team's config/inbox.yml sets media.remote: off. It cannot change the media setting.

markRead.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. Mark messages to the human read, as opening them in the Inbox does (`inbox()` row `unread` turns false; a message to anyone else is left alone). One transaction and at most one inbox change event. Resolves `{marked: n}` with how many unread human rows actually changed, counting duplicate ids once.

markUnread.purpose: Policy: restore unread state for human-directed messages using inbox:write, without changing archive or delivery state. Pass both org and team for a synced team, otherwise use the page team. Cross-team access uses the existing inbox:read:all-teams admission. One transaction, at most one inbox change event; resolves {marked:n}. The MCP twin is mark_unread. Architecture: a pane must hold an explicitly unread conversation against automatic read-on-display until the person opens it or chooses Jump to latest.

moveWorkspace.args: {teamKey: string, workspaceId: string, before?: string, after?: string}
moveWorkspace.purpose: Move a workspace card in its team's shared order, exactly as native card drag. Supply exactly one of before or after with another workspace id. Resolves {moved:boolean}; unknown ids and unchanged placements return false. The existing agentList delta carries the resulting order. MCP twin: reorder_workspace (move_workspace moves between machines).

openAgentInbox.purpose: Reveal a running agent and open its native inbox rail, as the row menu's Open inbox does. A handle without a running session rejects with unavailable: agent is not running. Presentation only.

openDiff.args: {repo: string, rev: string, path: string, storyId?: string, range?: {start: number, end: number, side?: 'after'}}
openDiff.purpose: await codesense.openDiff({repo,rev,path,storyId?,range?:{start,end,side?:after}}) → opened, commitNotLocal, worktreeRemoved, refused or unavailable. repo is a configured source slug, rev a local full/short commit SHA or WORKTREE (requires storyId); path is repository-relative. Opens a read-only source diff TAB; every tab read revalidates the attachment/worktree. Range is after-side, 1-based inclusive. repo:read required. Missing commits show This commit isn't on this Mac yet and a selectable git fetch origin <sha> command; CodeSense never fetches. Known stories offer Open in workspace using openWorkspace. Context-repo revisions are not supported.

openFile.purpose: Open a file in the CodeSense viewer. `path` is an absolute path (e.g. a `queryContext()` row's `path`) inside any synced team's content root, or a path relative to the page's own content root; with `team` it is relative to that team's content root in the page's org. A file in another team switches to that team first. Anything outside a known team content root rejects `refused:`, a missing file `not-found:`. `newTab:true` opens it in a tab of its own.

openLauncher.purpose: Opens the native launch sheet with a task filled in. Supply org and team for an admitted team; team-only uses the active org. Unknown or unadmitted teams reject. Presentation only: the person launches from the sheet. Architecture: the registry admits sessions:read. Policy (open): no extra prompt. Agents launch with open_workspace.

openMessage.deny_example: openMessage: no message 42 for the human in this team
openMessage.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. Open or focus an existing live HTML message tab for an inbox({scope:'to-human'}) row in the page team. Only HTML mail from an agent to the human is eligible; markdown/plain, agent-addressed, human-authored and unknown ids reject with an openMessage-prefixed error. Resolves `{opened: true, messageId}`. Preserves the current layout and marks nothing read; call markRead explicitly. The tab uses the message team bridge, action gate and preferences, exactly like native Open in tab. Render markdown/plain and show-message conversations in the page; use embedMessage for inline HTML.

openRoutineDraft.args: {name: string, task: string, when?: string, agent?: string}
openRoutineDraft.purpose: Opens a filled private routine draft under its agent. Without an agent, opens Agents to choose one. Presentation only: the person saves from the editor. Architecture: the registry admits sessions:read. Policy (open): no extra prompt. Agents create with routine_create.

openTab.deny_example: not-allowed: openTab targets generic (dir) workspaces only
openTab.purpose: Add a new terminal tab to an already-open GENERIC (dir) workspace and RETURN its addressable `{sessionId}`. The tab spawns at the workspace cwd; `agent:true` also launches the agent CLI into it so it can host `prompt`s. The tab-management half of a dashboard-driven dir workspace — refuses any non-generic / un-opened workspaceId.

openWorkspace.args: {storyId: string} | {target: {kind: 'story'|'epic'|'branch'|'dir', storyId?, session?, title?, agent?, team?, epic?, repo?, branch?, path?}, headed?: boolean, initialPrompt?: string, sessionMode?: 'new'|'focus'}
openWorkspace.purpose: Open a workspace — the generic open primitive. Back-compat `{storyId}`, or a `{target}` descriptor: `story` (worktree + agent), `epic` (prepare + assemble + agent, so `getEpicHandle()`/`sendToSession` reach it), `branch` (`{repo, branch}` — check out an arbitrary branch/PR into a managed worktree with the install layer, so `runSkill('code-review')` etc. run on it; adoptable into a CLI tab), or `dir` (`{path}` — open a plain CLI terminal rooted at ANY directory, the generic kind; new tabs inherit the cwd, and the tab-management verbs `openTab`/`sendToWorkspaceTab` drive it). The `epic` target opens the doc's OWN containing epic by default; passing an explicit `{team, epic}` (team = `orgSlug:teamName`, epic = a content-root-relative path) opens ANY managed epic. `headed` defaults `true`; `headed:false` runs the agent for ANY kind (story, epic, branch, or dir) in the BACKGROUND with no visible terminal (observe/adopt/kill from the Background agents panel). A headless epic/dir backgrounds ONE agent session (not the visible tile/shell the headed open surfaces). A `story` target also accepts an optional `session` (a lowercase slug) to open an ADDITIONAL named agent session on the SAME worktree (address it later via `sendToSession('storyId#session', …)`), and an optional `title` for the tab's display name. Every kind that launches an agent takes an optional `agent` — the agent that runs: a key (e.g. `builtin/codex`) or an id found in the team, then your private space, then the starters; omitted = `builtin/claude`. An unknown agent rejects `invalid: <reason>` and spawns nothing. `agent` applies to `story` (always), `branch` (the review agent, headed or background), `dir`, and `epic` ONLY via its HEADLESS agent (`headed:false`) — a HEADED epic open is a bare terminal with no auto-launched agent, so an agent there is rejected. Omitting `session` = the story's single main session, unchanged; fire several `openWorkspace` calls with different `session` labels to run e.g. architecture-review + ux-review + dev in parallel on one story. `initialPrompt` is the spawned agent's starting prompt in the SAME call (spawn → wait-live → submit into the agent, not the shell; a slash command such as `/review` works) — story-only (the only agent-backed session-returner that threads one today); epic, branch, and dir targets reject `initialPrompt`, and an empty/whitespace prompt is treated as absent (byte-identical spawn-only). `sessionMode` picks the launch's session semantics: `'focus'` (the DEFAULT, or omitted) REUSES + focuses the story's existing session — a repeat `openWorkspace` shows the same agent, takes no second cap slot (idempotent); `'new'` FORKS a fresh session even when one is live (a retry / parallel attempt — e.g. a second reviewer), auto-minted as `storyId#attempt-N` and legible in the Background agents panel as "StoryId · Attempt N". Each `'new'` fork costs one cap slot and rejects `busy` when saturated (never a silent focus-instead-of-fork). STORY-ONLY (like `initialPrompt`) — epic/branch/dir reject `'new'`; to get a second ADDRESSABLE session, prefer naming it via `session`. A `story` target also takes an optional `machineId`: where the story's workspace is created when it has none yet — a machine id from the team's machines, or `"local"` for This Mac. A new workspace is created on that machine (its worktree copied there) and its agent starts there; an existing workspace opens where it lives, and a `machineId` naming somewhere else rejects `unavailable:` (a workspace stays where it was created). Other kinds reject `machineId`.

postMessage.args: {to: string, text: string, onClick?: {type: 'goto-agent', agentId} | {type: 'open-file', path} | {type: 'show-message'}}
postMessage.purpose: Send a message from a dashboard pane into the active team's inbox. `to` is a role name (an agent id) OR the literal `"human"`; the message writes an inbox row AND (for a role) a pending wv_role_delivery row in one commit. Optional `onClick` is the per-message action the human-inbox UI honours when the human clicks the row: `goto-agent` focuses the agent's running terminal, `open-file` opens a path in the viewer, `show-message` (or omitted) opens the conversation in the native panel. The idempotency key is minted CodeSense-side so a double-click can't duplicate; rate-guarded under the send class.

react.args: {org?: string, team?: string, messageId: number, emoji: string, remove?: boolean}
react.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. React AS THE HUMAN to an `inbox()` message with one emoji, like a tapback: one reaction per (reactor, message, emoji), so reacting again with the same emoji takes it back (`remove: true` takes it back, `remove: false` makes sure it is there, omitted toggles). A reaction is not mail: it is not unread, wakes nobody and is not a reply. It appears in the row's `reactions` list and fires the inbox-changed event. Resolves `{status:'reacted', messageId, emoji, outcome: 'added'|'removed'|'unchanged'}` or `{status:'invalid', message}` (not exactly one emoji, unknown message).

readWorkspace.purpose: Read a file (or list a dir with a trailing `/`) STRICTLY within the doc's OWN directory subtree on a managed surface. The doc supplies only `path`; the extension whitelist, `..`/symlink confinement, and size/binary guards are all enforced CodeSense-side.

records.create.purpose: Create one record in a declared collection: generated-id collections such as Notes assign an id when it is omitted, and slug collections require id. Returns the record with its id. Scope and profile are bound to the frame. Writes allow 30 per 10 seconds per frame and collection; flush writes are exempt.

records.delete.purpose: Delete one record; confirmable. Agents can't delete notes: Notes allows human deletion only, and a page acts as the human. Private collections keep the history, so records.restore can bring it back. Scope and profile are bound to the frame. Writes allow 30 per 10 seconds per frame and collection; flush writes are exempt.

records.restore.purpose: Restore one private record to the revision commit from records.history; the restore is itself a new revision. Shared collections have no history. Scope and profile are bound to the frame. Writes allow 30 per 10 seconds per frame and collection; flush writes are exempt.

records.setFields.purpose: Set declared fields on one record without touching its body, e.g. Notes {title} or {pinned: true}. Pinned Notes list first, then most recently changed. Scope and profile are bound to the frame. Writes allow 30 per 10 seconds per frame and collection; flush writes are exempt.

records.write.args: {collection, id, body? | append? | patch?, base?, requestId?}
records.write.purpose: Replace, append to or patch one record's body; pass exactly one of body, append or patch. With base (the body you started from) a concurrent edit is merged: the result has merged: true and overlaps lists the regions both sides changed. Scope and profile are bound to the frame. Writes allow 30 per 10 seconds per frame and collection; flush writes are exempt.

replyAsHuman.args: {org?: string, team?: string, messageId: number, text: string, contentType?: 'plain'|'markdown'|'html', summary?: string}
replyAsHuman.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. Reply AS THE HUMAN to an `inbox()` message, exactly as the Inbox pane's reply does: the reply goes only to the message's `replyTo` when it has one (for `role:<id>`, queued as a pending delivery for that role), else to its sender, threaded under it, and the original is marked read. Resolves `{status:'sent', messageId}` or `{status:'invalid', message}` (blank text, unknown message).

routeToContext.purpose: Route a source-repo file into a CodeSense context layer.

routineCancel.purpose: Cancel this principal's live structured result runs for a routine, retaining last-good data.

routineRefresh.purpose: Explicitly refresh through existing routine admission, profile, overlap and runtime policy. Call it only from an explicit user action.

routineResult.purpose: Read a private cached structured routine result; never launches. Returns snapshot, latest_attempt, revision and schema_compatible.

routineStatus.purpose: Read cached routine result and latest attempt status, without launches.

runPrompt.purpose: Drive a prompt into an ALREADY-LIVE story session (supersedes the retired `fireSkill`). `target` is a story session handle — a bare `storyId` (the main session) or the compound `storyId#<label>` (a named session, e.g. `DEMO-11#architecture-review`) — resolved CodeSense-side, so a raw session id from the doc can never redirect the write. `prompt` is ARBITRARY text (a slash-command like `/bmad-code-review {storyPath}` is just one shape): the single token `{storyPath}` is filled CodeSense-side with the story's managed absolute path, and the line is submitted to the agent as is. It does NOT spawn and does NOT take an agent/command/model: it drives the agent that is already running. A handle with no live session rejects `unavailable:` (never spawns, never redirects) — open it first with `openWorkspace` (which owns spawn + `session` + `agent` + `initialPrompt`).

runSkill.purpose: DEPRECATED → prefer `runPrompt` (a prompt into a real, observable session) or `openWorkspace({headed:false, initialPrompt})`. Runs a REGISTERED skill on the user's agent CLI (detached, headless) with tool use ENABLED + multi-turn — the write-capable sibling of `analyze`. Bounded by its own concurrency cap.

sendAsHuman.args: {org?: string, team?: string, to: string, text: string, contentType?: 'plain'|'markdown'|'html', onClick?: {type: 'goto-agent', agentId} | {type: 'open-file', path} | {type: 'show-message'}, attachFile?: string, replyTo?: string, summary?: string, inReplyTo?: number}
sendAsHuman.purpose: Pass both {org, team} to act in a synced team; omit both to keep the page team. Cross-team access requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant, included by the default open policy. Send a message AS THE HUMAN. `to` is a running session (a `sessions()` handle; the mail lands in that session's own inbox and its inbox waiter wakes it) or, failing that, a role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id) queued in the page's team for whichever instance claims it. `contentType` defaults to markdown; `html` is sanitized in the inbox. `attachFile` is a team-content path shown as an attachment card. `replyTo` is where replies go instead of to the human, like an email Reply-To (only there): a running session's handle, `'human'`, or `'role:<agent id>'` (that role's durable queue, so the answer outlives the session that writes it). `summary` is one plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as the message's one-line gist in the Inbox and lists; set it for html and long markdown. Resolves `{status:'sent', messageId, deliveryId?}` (`deliveryId` for a role) or `{status:'invalid', message}` (blank text, no recipient, a replyTo session that is not running, or an unknown inReplyTo). `inReplyTo` threads the reply under an existing message in this team, sends only to `to`, and marks the answered message read only if addressed to the human.

sendPrompt.purpose: Type into any running agent by its handle, locally or on a remote machine, without a dashboard launch controller. Submits by default; submit:false types without Enter. Returns {status, submitted, machine, code, message}; a rejected command returns status:invalid. An unknown delivery may have arrived: never retry it automatically. Agents prompt running agents with send_to_session; this is the person's typed send from a page.

sendToSession.purpose: Inject a chat turn into a story's already-running agent session.

sendToWorkspaceTab.purpose: Deliver text to a specific generic-workspace tab addressed by the `sessionId` returned from `openTab`. `command` submits to the shell; `prompt` injects into a verified-live agent (refuses `no-agent-in-tab` when the tab hosts no live agent — a prompt NEVER lands in a bare shell). Addressable ONLY for a tab of an OPEN generic workspace (a story/branch/epic agent session is never reachable through this verb).

setField.args: {path: string, field: string, value: string | number | boolean | Array<string|number|boolean> | null} | {path: string, fields: Record<string, …>}
setField.purpose: Write top-level frontmatter keys of a content file (`.md`, or a mapped `cs:*` meta in `.html`) inside a team or private content root: `value: null` removes the key, numbers/booleans are written as YAML numbers/booleans, lists as block lists. One atomic write that changes only those keys' bytes; `subscribeContext` pages re-query. Field names are plain keys (letters, digits, `_`, `-`); objects and multi-line strings reject `invalid:`, a path outside every content root rejects `refusing to edit metadata:`.

setHumanStatus.purpose: Set the human's status in the page's team (what agents read with get_human_status to decide whether to ping): `online`, `away` (short break), `busy` (heads-down; only critical pings), `offline` (out). `note` is a short free-text hint (<=200 chars). Resolves the new `{status, note?, updatedAtMs}`; pages get `codesense:agents-changed`.

setModelRate.args: {modelPrefix, effectiveFrom (YYYY-MM-DD, local), inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok?, long?: {fromTokens, inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok?}} (USD per million tokens)
setModelRate.purpose: Request a model price from a local day. Reductions and prices for unknown models stay pending until a person reviews and accepts the exact request in the affected agent's or routine's Spend cap block in the native app; neither pages nor MCP can approve. Rate increases apply immediately. `cacheReadPerMtok` is the cache-read price where it is not 0.1x input; `long` prices a call whose prompt (input, cache reads and cache writes) is over `fromTokens`. A rate is the whole price from its day on: a price it leaves out falls back to its default (cache reads at 0.1x input, one price at every prompt length), even where the earlier rate named one. Every price is above 0 and at most 100,000; `fromTokens` is a whole number from 1; `null` is the same as leaving a price out; an unknown key is refused with `invalid:`, so a misspelled price is never dropped. Usage already priced from the rate table is corrected to it; a cost the CLI reported is never changed. Returns the number of costs changed immediately; a pending request returns 0 and does not change effective prices. `codesense.modelRates()` shows effective rates, not pending requests. Pending requests and exact native approval are shown in the affected agent's or routine's Spend cap block, through agentList. Page and MCP requests use source 'set by an agent'; native acceptance uses 'set by the user'. The MCP tool `set_model_rate` follows the same rules.

setPrefs.args: Record<string, JSON> (a key set to null is removed)
setPrefs.purpose: Merge keys into THIS dashboard's own settings (read them back with `codesense.prefs()`), kept in the user's app state across restarts — a frame's localStorage is not (its origin changes every launch). One entry per dashboard instance, chosen by the app: a pane's own file, a centre dashboard's path, an inbox message. A team copy and a private copy never share; nothing is written to team content. 16 KB per dashboard (`too-large:` past it), 512 KB for all of a user's dashboards (the least recently written are dropped first); values must be plain JSON (`invalid:` for a Map, Set, BigInt, Date, function or NaN). Its own runaway budget, 30 calls per 10 s (`denied: prefs budget`), separate from the metadata write budget, and no audit line: it touches only this dashboard's own entry.

setStatus.purpose: Set a scanned doc's `status` frontmatter. The batch form (`path[]`) applies best-effort and resolves to a per-item result array.

setUiState.purpose: Persist host-owned shared slot UI state and publish a versioned delta echoing requestId. Uses the app-state store with its own namespace and the same limits as prefs.

stopSession.purpose: Stop ANY live session by the `handle` a `sessions()` row carries, as the Agents panel's Stop does (a dispatched Weft worker is marked needs-attention first; frees its concurrency slot, writes one audit line). Idempotent: a handle with no live session is a no-op, so a page can stop defensively. Resolves `{stopped: true}` once the stop is delivered; `onSessions` then sees the roster change (a Weft worker's durable row stays listed).

analyze: invoke('analyze') uses the configured agent CLI; handle unavailable, timeout and busy errors, and render model output as text.

actions.call: CS.act(name, {id, choice?}) resolves the declared action result or rejects its error code. id is an ASCII alphanumeric first character followed by at most 63 letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen; slash and .. are refused. It must resolve uniquely in this dashboard's team and match the manifest. No text, paths, prompts or extra keys. Calls are sent once and never retried; on timeout inspect activity before deciding to try again.
actions.declare: actions maps a name to {verb, who: owner, match?, max_per_hour?, max_running?}. setFields takes fixed scalar fields (null removes a key) or choices mapping a declared choice to fixed fields. max_running applies to launched agents; routines retain their own admission/overlap policy. launchAgent takes agent, prompt (only {id}, <=500 characters), mode headless or visible-unfocused. runRoutine takes routine and fixed vars (only {id}, <=500 characters each). Agents/routines must exist. Only the owner can run actions; viewers watch activity. who: viewers is parsed for compatibility but does not permit mutation access.
actions.frames: page to relay: act {v:1, op:act, aid, action, args} -> acted {v:1, op:acted, aid, ok, result|error}; relay to Mac: x {v:1,t:x,id,dashboard,action,args,by} -> xa {v:1,t:xa,id,ok,result|error}. The relay stamps by; the page cannot choose it. Subscribe to actions for the last 50 calls and session/routine progress. Activity exposes role and share id, never an email.
actions.limits: Defaults 5 successful calls/hour and 2 running agents per action; hard maximum 30/hour and 4 running. Relay cap 10 calls/minute/session, 1024-byte args. Errors: not_declared, not_allowed, invalid_args, not_found, rate_limited, busy, failed, mac_offline, timeout.
actions.starter: create_dashboard {template: bug-triage, agent: <agent_list id>} writes queryContext bugs, three owner actions, activity and the shared terminal view. Without agent it omits Work it and explains how to add it. control: true optionally enables owner terminal control.

verbs.description: Built-in owner-only plain-text send or reply within the dashboard team; no action declaration
verbs.name: ownerMessage

verbs.description: Built-in owner-only emoji reaction (tapback) on a message of the dashboard team's inbox, one of 😂 ❤️ 👍 😮 🎉 🔥; toggles; no action declaration
verbs.name: ownerReact

verbs.description: Built-in owner-only: marks messages to the human read in the dashboard team's inbox, 1 to 200 ids per call, idempotent; every id must be a message to the human in this team, else not_found; no action declaration
verbs.name: ownerMarkRead

verbs.description: Owner-only plain-text send to a declared recipient set
verbs.name: sendMessage

verbs.description: Set declared metadata fields on a validated team file
verbs.name: setFields

verbs.description: Launch the declared agent on a validated team id
verbs.name: launchAgent

verbs.description: Fire the declared routine with fixed variables
verbs.name: runRoutine

hosted.args: The dashboard sets what a query shares; a viewer's args only narrow it. sessionUsage takes {sinceMs?, untilMs?, sessionId?, limit?, cursor?}, plus story? (one story id: only the sessions spent on it) when the dashboard shares story and cwd? when it shares cwd; a dashboard that lists `live: {fields: {sessionUsage: [story]}}` gets each row's story {id, title, status, epic} or null, never a path, so a page can group usage by story; sessions {launchedBy?}, setup {} (no args; a fixed allow-list of attribution and capture status), runs {limit?}, queryContext {match?: {field: value | [values]}, sort?: [field | -field], limit?, groupBy?, cursor?} on the fields the dashboard shares, always in one org and team: the ones whose context repo folder holds the dashboard folder (the org and team query_context lists for a file there), worked out when publish_dashboard runs. A dashboard outside a team's context repo, or published while CodeSense could not tell its team, gets answer_failed. Unknown or wrong-typed args give query_invalid. Rows are capped at 500 (sessionUsage and runs default to 50); see answer_size for the 256 KB cap.
hosted.chrome: chrome: none (default), full or minimal. With none the viewer draws nothing over the page, for the owner and for viewers: no bar, no badge. The page gets the state through CS.viewer(cb) ({role, mac, mac_seen_at, updated_at, stale, display}) and shows its own as-of time, Mac status and offline or stale notice; CS.endOwnerAccess() ends the owner's access (owner only, from a click). A page that has not called CS.viewer within 3 s gets the viewer's own offline and stale notice, so a page that never adopted the SDK is not silent. Ended access, a page that kept leaving the dashboard, and a refused link are always drawn by the viewer; a page cannot block or hide them or the server ending access. A dashboard with no stored presentation becomes none the next time the viewer serves it, with no republish. A stored full or minimal is kept until the next publish: older manifests with install: commonly stored full, so republish those to drop the bar. chrome: full shows the viewer bar (title, Page updated, Mac status, and for the owner End owner access); minimal hides it for viewers (the owner always sees the full header), with notices and the live stale banner still shown; show your own as-of time. A chromeless page can imitate CodeSense UI: never ask a viewer for a password or code in a dashboard. Sign-out and the dashboards a viewer can see live on the share site's /account page, outside the page.
hosted.declare: List the queries the page uses in dashboard.yml: `live: {queries: [sessionUsage, runs]}`; `queries: []` shows only whether the owner's Mac is online; `queries: all` allows every query below, now and later. A person confirms a new or wider list once in the CodeSense app; until they do, publish_dashboard publishes the page without live data and returns live: pending_confirmation. Only declared queries are answered; any other gets query_not_declared. Editing the block of a published dashboard takes effect within seconds while CodeSense is open, without publishing again; removing it turns live data off. Secrets (publisher tokens, API keys, Keychain) are never answered.

embeds.declare: live: {queries: [queryContext], fields: {queryContext: [status, title, sprint]}, embeds: {queries: [queryContext], fields: {queryContext: [status, title, sprint]}, run: owner}}. Every name in embeds must already be declared by the page itself and every field must be one the page shares: an embed never sees more than the page. A query with no field list in embeds gets its defaults, narrowed to what the page shares. embeds is part of the block's sha, so an edit is saved like any other live edit. An unknown key under embeds is refused.
embeds.grant_file: publish writes cs-embeds.json from the saved block ({v, sha, queries, streams, fields, run}); it is never read from the folder and the name cannot be listed in publish.files. The page fetches it with fetch('cs-embeds.json'). A missing or unreadable file means no embeds. Older CodeSense versions ignore the key, so the file is absent and nothing runs.
embeds.limits: Per message 10 reads a minute and 4 subscriptions: one-shot calls and every recurring poll tick count against the same 10, so a message that over-subscribes hears rate_limited on the ticks it cannot pay for; across the page 30 asks a minute and 2 in flight; identical subscriptions share one upstream poll (at most every 15 s) and each subscribing message pays for its own tick. Envelopes over 16 KB are dropped. Answers are cut to the granted fields before the message sees them.
embeds.mac_side: queryContext accepts the local SDK shape, as narrowing only: where.kinds, filters with eq and in on shared fields, select within the shared fields. The team and layer stay the dashboard's.
embeds.message_api: Inside the message: window.codesense.queryContext(q), subscribeContext(q, cb(result, err)), inbox(args), has(name), ready(). openFile rejects with unavailable (it needs the Mac app). Errors carry .code: not_declared, unavailable, rate_limited, invalid_args, mac_offline, no_answer, failed.
page_steps: fetch('cs-embeds.json'); if it is missing, show the message as a card or static text
await CS.ready(); build the frame only when CSEmbed.mayRun(grant, CS.role()) is true, else show the card
create the frame with sandbox="allow-scripts" only and srcdoc = CSEmbed.buildSrcdoc(body, {head: themeStyle}), where themeStyle defines the --cs-* tokens for light and dark (see theme)
create the pool over CS.query (upstream.query(name, args) returns the answer), create the forwarder with role: CS.role, and window.addEventListener('message', forwarder.handle)
call forwarder.setVisible(false) for a collapsed or off-screen message
embeds.risk: With run: owner or run: everyone, agent-authored JavaScript runs on those people's devices with the same trust as on the Mac. It can read everything embeds grants and, through WebRTC (which a page cannot block), it can reveal the device's IP address to a host of its choosing. With everyone, you vouch for your agents' messages to the people you invited. Leave run: none if that is not what you want; no run is the safe default.
embeds.run: embeds.run says for whom a message's own scripts run: none (the default: nobody, messages stay static), owner (only the signed-in owner) or everyone (every invited viewer). run needs at least one query or stream in embeds. Viewers and owners alike can only read what embeds grants: nothing in this pipe acts, so a viewer can never send, reply, mark, open or change anything through a message.
embeds.theme: The host page must supply the --cs-* theme tokens to the message frame, for light and dark, as the in-app Inbox does. A message written on the Mac styles itself with var(--cs-fg), var(--cs-bg) and the rest; a frame without them falls back to the message's own defaults (often light text, written for a dark app) and can render unreadably, for example light text on a white bubble. The tokens: --cs-bg, --cs-fg, --cs-muted-fg, --cs-border, --cs-surface, --cs-accent, --cs-link, --cs-success, --cs-warning, --cs-danger (and --cs-font-sans). Pass them through the head option of buildSrcdoc, with color: var(--cs-fg) on the body, for example CSEmbed.buildSrcdoc(body, {head: '<style>:root{--cs-bg:#fff;--cs-fg:#1d1d1f;--cs-muted-fg:#6e6e73;--cs-border:#d2d2d7;--cs-surface:#f5f5f7;--cs-accent:#0a64d6;--cs-link:#0a64d6;--cs-success:#1a7f37;--cs-warning:#9a6700;--cs-danger:#cf222e}@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root{--cs-bg:#161618;--cs-fg:#e6e6e6;--cs-muted-fg:#9a9aa0;--cs-border:#333338;--cs-surface:#1f1f22;--cs-accent:#7ab7ff;--cs-link:#7ab7ff;--cs-success:#3fb950;--cs-warning:#d29922;--cs-danger:#f85149}}body{margin:0;color:var(--cs-fg)}</style>'}). The head runs under the frame's closed CSP (inline styles are allowed, nothing else loads), so put styles in it, never links.
embeds.toolkit: cs-embed.js (version comment `// cs-embed 1`) is the one source for the page side and the message side. Copy it next to cs-live.js and list it in publish.files. CSEmbed.mayRun(grant, CS.role()) says whether to build the frame at all; CSEmbed.createPool(upstream) bounds the page's asks; CSEmbed.createForwarder({pool, grant, role: CS.role, frame}) is the only path from the frame; CSEmbed.buildSrcdoc(body) wraps the message with a closed CSP and the message-side window.codesense.
embeds.what: Lets the HTML messages an agent sends to the owner run live inside a published dashboard (the Inbox page, say): the page puts each message in a sandboxed frame and forwards the message's codesense queries (queryContext, subscribeContext, inbox) to its own live pipe. The page's publisher grants what a message may read; the message never grants itself anything.

hosted.fields: Share more with `live: {fields: {queryContext: [status, title, priority], runs: [summary], sessionUsage: [story]}}`: for queryContext the frontmatter keys returned (default status, title, type, owner, updated); for the others the optional fields listed under each query. They are on as soon as the block is saved.

guide.answer_size: An answer is at most 256 KB as JSON. The list queries (sessionUsage, sessions, runs, inbox, queryContext) keep the first rows that fit, measured as sent (after redaction), and cut from the end of their own order: sessionUsage newest activity first, runs newest first, inbox newest first, sessions in handle order (not by recency), queryContext the sort you asked for (or its default). A limit of 500 is safe to ask. Every list answers as an object, and when the Mac had to cut rows, by the limit or by size, the object carries truncated: true, returned (the rows sent) and total (the rows before the cut), the same on every list: runs answers {runs: [...]}, sessionUsage {sessions, days, totals, total}, sessions {sessions}, inbox {messages}, queryContext {rows} (its total and truncated are always present; sessionUsage and queryContext pages always carry returned and total too). The totals and days of sessionUsage still cover everything. Test truncated and say so on the page. To read past the cut, page: sessionUsage and queryContext answer nextCursor when rows follow the last one sent (it points after that row even when the cut was by size); pass it back as cursor with the same other args to get the next page, until nextCursor is absent. A cursor from other args is refused (query_invalid). Every page carries total (all matches), returned (the rows on this page) and truncated (this page is not everything); sessionUsage total, totals and days count the current matches on every page. During a walk a session that becomes active moves to the first page; a walk is complete when its distinct sessionIds equal total, otherwise walk again from page 1 through continuation, merging by sessionId, up to 2 recovery rewalks; after that report the truthful latest N of M. queryContext's pages read one index snapshot, kept 30 s after each page and 120 s at most; past that, or after the Mac's app restarted, the cursor answers stale_cursor, so restart without a cursor. Other lists have no cursor: sessionUsage also takes a window (sinceMs, untilMs); runs takes only limit, sessions only launchedBy, and inbox has no time or cursor (narrow it with scope, agentId, sessionId or role); queryContext narrows with match, filters or where. Say on the page when it shows part of the list. Rough bytes per row: sessionUsage 600 to 850 (more with several models), sessions 350, runs 450, inbox 400 plus the text of each message when fields.inbox lists text, queryContext 150 plus about 30 per frontmatter field; the totals and days of sessionUsage and the rest of the answer are counted first. Only a single row or value over the cap fails, as answer_too_large.
guide.fresh_data: A dashboard is as fresh as its listed files. An agent or a routine rewrites a data file (for example a routine that calls session_usage and writes data/usage.json); there is no built-in usage source. While CodeSense is open on the owner's Mac, a change to a listed file is pushed about 60 s after the last write, and every 15 minutes the Mac checks in or pushes. Viewers see 'Page updated N minutes ago' from server time: when the files were last published (a check-in alone does not change it, nor does a live answer; a live page can show its answers' answered_at), and a stale warning when the Mac has not checked in for 30 minutes. The viewer checks for a new version every 60 s and reloads the page. Adding a file means adding it to publish.files.
guide.layout: One folder holds the dashboard: dashboard.yml, index.html (the page viewers open first), any other pages, scripts, stylesheets, images and data files, e.g. index.html, runs.html, app.js, style.css, data/summary.json. Only files listed in dashboard.yml leave the Mac; the rest stay local. Put the folder inside a team's context repo (under that team's content folder): CodeSense shows it there, and live queryContext reads that team's context. Outside a team's context repo CodeSense may not show it and every queryContext answer fails; create_dashboard warns about it.
guide.live_answers: A page gets live answers only through live_page_api. Declared live queries are asked of the owner's Mac through codesense.ai while the Mac is connected (CodeSense open, a published dashboard with a live block). A person must confirm a new or wider live block once in the CodeSense app (publish_dashboard returns live: pending_confirmation until they do, and live data stays paused); a narrower or removed block takes effect within seconds. Answers are read-only and redacted, at most 256 KB, 10 s timeout, 60 asks per minute per viewer session. When the Mac is offline the last answer to the same query and args is returned with source 'cache' and its answered_at time, and the viewer shows 'Live data unavailable, showing data from N minutes ago' above the page until a live answer comes; with no cached answer the error is mac_offline. The cache is deleted on unpublish, when a query leaves the list, and for a query whose live.args pins change. Pin refusals never use the cache. Cached and in-flight answers must match the current query pin revision and the viewer permission computed on the Mac. Selector queries use a cache fallback only while the Mac is offline, never for online rate limits, timeout, failure or oversized answers. An authoritative arg_not_allowed or not_approved discards that exact cached answer and prevents pending older answers from restoring it.

live_errors.access_ended: the viewer's access ended (session expired or the viewer was removed, or the dashboard was unpublished); the page's subscriptions stop and the viewer shows the request form
live_errors.answer_failed: the Mac's answer failed, the relay failed, or the request did not reach codesense.ai, and there is no cached answer (HTTP 502, or anything unexpected)
live_errors.answer_too_large: the answer is over 256 KB even as one row or one value, and there is no cached answer (HTTP 502). The list queries cut their rows to fit instead, so this is rare: narrow the query (fewer rows or a shorter window) and show "That answer is too big for a shared dashboard; narrow the query (fewer rows or a shorter window)."
live_errors.arg_not_allowed: a pinned arg is missing or outside live.args, or a viewer asks storyChanges without a storyId pin, storyTotals without a storyIds pin or whyLine without a repo pin (HTTP 403). Never served from cache
live_errors.bad_request: a malformed request: v is not 1, id is not a 1-100 character string or a number, op is not query/subscribe/unsubscribe, query is not a name, args is not a plain object, every_s is not a non-negative number, or subscribe reuses the id of an active subscription
live_errors.busy: CS.endOwnerAccess() while an earlier call is still waiting for the server
live_errors.failed: CS.endOwnerAccess() could not reach the server; owner access is unchanged
live_errors.mac_busy: every one of the owner's Mac's 8 query slots stayed taken for 3 s and there is no cached answer (HTTP 503). CS.query and CS.queryAll ask again after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 8 s before they reject with it
live_errors.mac_offline: the owner's Mac is not connected and there is no cached answer (HTTP 503)
live_errors.mac_timeout: the Mac did not answer within 10 s of starting the query and there is no cached answer (HTTP 504)
live_errors.needs_gesture: CS.endOwnerAccess() without a recent click or tap in the page; call it from a click handler
live_errors.not_owner: CS.endOwnerAccess() from a viewer: only the dashboard's owner can end owner access
live_errors.post_to_own_window: the page posted the request to parent instead of its own window; nothing was asked
live_errors.query_invalid: args over 2 KB or not accepted by the query: an unknown or wrong-typed arg (HTTP 422)
live_errors.query_not_declared: the query is not in the dashboard's live list (HTTP 403), or the Mac answered not_approved
live_errors.rate_limited: over 60 asks a minute for this viewer session, or 4 already waiting for it at codesense.ai with no cached answer (HTTP 429); in the shell: a 21st subscription on the page, or a request when 64 are already queued
live_errors.stale_cursor: a queryContext cursor whose index snapshot is gone: a walk's pages read one snapshot, kept 30 s after each page and 120 s at most, and a cursor from an earlier app run is stale too (HTTP 409). Restart paging without a cursor; CS.queryAll and CS.subscribeAll do it silently. Never served from cache

guide.live_page_api: Built in the viewer shell. The page posts to its own window, not to parent: postMessage({cs:'live', v:1, op:'query', id, query, args}, '*'); op:'subscribe' adds every_s (repeats at max(every_s, 15) s, at most 20 per page); op:'unsubscribe' with the id. id is a string of 1 to 100 characters or a number; args is a plain object. At most 4 requests per page run at once; up to 64 more wait, and beyond that the request gets rate_limited. Replies come from parent (check e.source === parent): {cs:'live', v:1, id, ok:true, source:'live'|'cache', answered_at, server_time, answer} or {cs:'live', v:1, id, ok:false, error} (see live_errors). Presence arrives as {cs:'live', v:1, op:'presence', mac:'online'|'offline'|'unknown', mac_seen_at} when the page has loaded and again on each status check (every 60 s); with chrome: full the viewer also shows 'Owner's Mac: online', 'offline since <time>' or 'status unknown' in its top bar. The default, chrome: none, draws nothing: the viewer sends {cs:'live', v:1, op:'viewer', role:'owner'|'viewer', mac, mac_seen_at, updated_at, stale, display} on hello and on each change (CS.viewer in the toolkit; display is the signed-in viewer's own email, or owner); posting {cs:'live', v:1, op:'viewer_sub'} tells the viewer the page shows offline and stale itself, otherwise the viewer shows its own notice after 3 s. {cs:'live', v:1, op:'end_owner', id} (owner only, from a click) ends owner access on the server and the reply is {cs:'live', v:1, id, ok}. A new page ends the old page's subscriptions. In the CodeSense viewer on the Mac nothing answers these messages, so give the page a fallback (the create_dashboard starter times out after 15 s and says so).

manifest.example:
slug: ai-usage
title: AI usage
publish:
  state: draft
  visibility: private
  files:
    - index.html
    - runs.html
    - app.js
    - style.css
    - data/summary.json
live:
  queries: [sessions, runs, storyChanges, whyLine]
  args:
    storyChanges: {storyId: [DEMO-46, {epic: DEMO}]}
    whyLine: {repo: [acme/app]}
  fields:
    runs: [summary]
manifest.live: Optional. Absent: a static dashboard. queries: [] shows only whether the owner's Mac is online; queries: [names] or all allows live answers (see declare, queries, fields and pins above).
manifest.publish.entry: Decided but not built: the manifest has no entry field yet. The hosted viewer opens index.html, else the first .html in sorted order. Always have an index.html.
manifest.publish.files: Every file the pages use, as relative paths inside the folder (no leading /, no ./ or .., no backslash, no symlink or hard link, each listed once). At most 50 files, 5 MB each, 25 MB in all. Types: html, css, js, json, csv, txt, png, jpg/jpeg, webp, gif. No SVG and no font files.
manifest.publish.state: draft or published. publish_dashboard sets published, unpublish_dashboard sets draft; do not edit it by hand.
manifest.publish.visibility: private or team. team is reserved and is currently the same as private: only invited viewers get in.
manifest.slug: 3 to 40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -; the address is https://<dash host>/d/<slug>. Unique across publishers (slug taken: choose another).
manifest.title: 1 to 200 characters after trimming; shown in the viewer's top bar.

guide.not_built: Decided but not built: publish does not yet scan pages for references to unlisted or outside files, and it does not yet report linked dashboards that are unpublished. Today such a reference just fails to load in the hosted viewer, so check the references yourself.
rules: Load data with fetch("data/<name>.json") relative to the page. In the hosted viewer the page runs in a sandbox with no network: fetch of a listed file is answered by the viewer, fetch of an unlisted file gets a 404, fetch of any web address fails. XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, cookies and localStorage do not work there.
Reference only listed files:

No bridge calls. window.codesense, codesense.act and codesense.<verb>( are for pages inside the CodeSense app; publish_dashboard refuses a page that has one and names the file and line. Live data comes from the live block instead.
Links between pages are relative (<a href="runs.html">) and must point at a listed .html page; in-page #anchors work. A link to an unlisted file shows 'That link is not in this dashboard.'

Outside links (http and https) are allowed and open in a new tab; nothing is fetched for them at publish. A link to another dashboard is an outside link to https://<dash host>/d/<slug>: the viewer needs its own invite to that dashboard, and publishing one dashboard never publishes another.
Only a real click follows a link (at most 10 per 5 s). A page that navigates itself by script is rebuilt, and stopped after 3 tries.
Each page load is a fresh document: keep state in the URL fragment or reload it from data files.
Per page the viewer allows 8 data requests at once and 25 MB of data read in all, so read the data once on load instead of polling; the viewer reloads the page itself when a new version arrives.
guide.share: share_dashboard {dashboard, add?: [emails], remove?: [emails]}: add gives access, remove takes it away and ends those viewers' sessions at once, neither just lists the viewers; every call returns {slug, viewers, notOnList}. Invite emails are reviewed before they are sent. To see the dashboard yourself, add the owner's own address.
guide.start: create_dashboard {folder, slug, title, pages?, data?, live?, template?, control?} writes a folder that already follows every rule below. Use template mission-control for an agent list and terminal, or workspaces to group by workspace; both accept control: true (default false). Then fill any data files, publish_dashboard, share_dashboard. Publishing is in beta release builds and internal builds with the dashboard-publish feature.
guide.viewers: A viewer opens the one-time link from the email (valid 15 minutes, single use) and gets a session for that dashboard only; it ends after viewers.session_days (90 by default) without a visit, and 90 days after sign-in at the latest. They see the title, 'Page updated N minutes ago' (when the files were last published), a stale warning when the Mac stopped checking in, the pages, and, for a dashboard with a live block, 'Owner's Mac: online', 'offline since <time>' or 'status unknown'. Anyone else gets the same not-found page with a form to request a link. Viewers cannot change anything. If the dashboard sets live.embeds.run: everyone, an agent's HTML messages on it run their scripts on the viewer's device; they can read only what live.embeds grants, can reveal the device's IP address and can never act. Without run (the default) viewers see static messages only (see hosted.embeds).
you_can: build a small multi-page web app: several pages, shared scripts and styles, images, JSON, CSV or text data
use any JavaScript library you put in the folder and list
keep the data fresh by having an agent or routine rewrite the data files while CodeSense is open
link to any web page or to another dashboard (opens in a new tab)
show live, read-only answers from the owner's Mac for declared catalog queries (sessionUsage, sessions, runs, queryContext), with the last answer shown when the Mac is offline
list the team's agents and open workspaces live and watch an agent's terminal as it runs (streams workspaces, terminals, terminal; create_dashboard {template: "workspaces"} writes a ready dashboard)
take it down with unpublish_dashboard and publish again later
you_cannot: call the CodeSense bridge (window.codesense, act) from a published page
reach the network from a hosted page: no fetch to web addresses, no XMLHttpRequest, no WebSocket, no CDN scripts or web fonts
load or link files that are not listed or that live outside the folder
use SVG or font files, more than 50 files, a file over 5 MB or more than 25 MB in all
write anything as an invited viewer (only the owner can type into terminals)
type into a terminal unless you are the owner and the dashboard allows control (live.control: owner), and only after Take control in the viewer's top bar
send invite emails yourself: they are reviewed before they are sent
set a different entry page yet (publish.entry is decided, not built)

install.declare: In dashboard.yml add install: {name: Family brief, short_name: Brief, icon: images/icon.png, theme_color: {light: '#f7f6f3', dark: '#201e1c'}}. The icon must be a .png path in publish.files. install and chrome take effect on the next push or scheduled check-in; removing install removes home-screen metadata.
install.icon: Use a square, opaque PNG of at least 180 x 180; 512 x 512 is better for both iOS and Android. iOS rounds corners itself and fills transparency with black. Do not draw rounded corners or a shadow. Keep the mark inside the middle 70%, without words. Size and opacity are advice, not enforced.
install.name: name is 1 to 64 characters; short_name is optional and at most 30. Keep short_name to 12 characters or fewer. If name is longer than that, set a short_name. The document title stays the dashboard title.
install.offline: Offline use is not supported; installation does not add a service worker or cache the dashboard for offline use.
install.theme_color: Set theme_color to your page background: light and dark are #rrggbb. Defaults are #f5f5f7 light and #161618 dark. The shell owns the safe-area padding; do not add it again in the page.

page_api.error: {cs:'live', v:1, id, ok:false, error} with error arg_not_allowed | query_not_declared | mac_offline | mac_busy | mac_timeout | query_invalid | stale_cursor | answer_failed | answer_too_large | rate_limited | bad_request | access_ended | post_to_own_window | not_owner | needs_gesture | busy | failed (when each happens: guide.live_errors)
page_api.result: {cs:'live', v:1, id, ok:true, source:'live'|'cache', answered_at, server_time, answer} (times are server unix seconds; source 'cache' is the last answer, shown while the Mac is offline)
page_api.subscribe: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'subscribe', id, query, args, every_s} (repeats at max(every_s, 15) s; at most 20 per page)

hosted.pins: Narrow hosted queries with live.args: {storyChanges: {storyId: [DEMO-46]}, whyLine: {repo: [acme/app]}}. Each declared query's known arg takes 1–64 literal strings or integers, sorted and deduped. Matching is exact by JSON type and value (5 differs from "5"); every pinned arg must be sent, including optional args such as whyLine.rev. Unpinned args stay open. Pins apply to owners too. Viewers require storyChanges.storyId, storyTotals.storyIds and whyLine.repo pins; share_dashboard add refuses until those pins exist, even with queries: all. Owner-only publish and unpinned owner asks stay allowed. Unknown live keys (including arg instead of args) are refused. Edits take effect when the watcher saves the block, without republishing; until then asks fail closed. Requests carry live_args; the share server refuses before relay or cache and deletes a query's cache when its pins change. Only storyChanges.storyId and storyTotals.storyIds also accept {epic: DEMO} or {team: web} selectors, mixed with literals. storyTotals.storyIds is a list: every id in it must pass the pin. Selectors require a known saved team scope at publish; team must equal that saved team. At ask time the Mac resolves current stories using the context-query engine in that scope (parent_epic/epic or epic folder), and refuses unknown or foreign stories, a moved dashboard scope, or an index that is not ready. A selector satisfies the viewer pin rule. The share server checks literal args and leaves selector args to the Mac. Pin changes prune the cache. While the Mac is offline, the last answer it approved under the current pins can still be served, even for a story that has since left the epic; an answer the Mac refused never is. Online failures never serve a selector cache fallback. Pins cover queries only, not streams. The starter sends the first literal for each pinned arg of its selected query, preserving JSON types. A selector-only arg gets a named placeholder in app.js, with configuration guidance in the rendered error, warnings and nextSteps.

queries.describe: The dashboard team's human inbox, session inboxes and role queues
queries.name: inbox
queries.shares: {messages: [{messageId, from, fromName, summary, kind, createdAt, unread, inReplyTo, delivery?: {state}}], humanUnread}. No bodies unless fields: text is declared. fields: meta adds to, toName, replyTo?, replyToName? and contentType (plain, markdown, html or null). fields: media adds attachments [{kind: image, alt, state (cached, pending, blocked or failed), mime?, sha256?, width?, height?, bytes?}], never a source URL, host or failure reason. fields: reactions adds reactions [{emoji, count, mine}] (mine: the human reacted), never who reacted. fields: faces adds sender: {face} to the rows whose sender wears one: {sha256, mime: image/png, width, height} for a picture (its bytes come from the media query), {emoji} or {colour} (#rrggbb); only for senders of the rows returned, no roster. Team fixed by the dashboard; args scope (to-human, to-agents, all, or human: only messages to or from the human, filtered on the Mac so no agent-to-agent mail leaves it), agentId, sessionId, role and limit only narrow; any other scope is query_invalid. At most 500 rows, newest first; a list cut by that limit or by size carries truncated, returned and total. Reads mark nothing read. Redacted

queries.describe: One image cached on this Mac for a message in the dashboard team's inbox, in chunks
queries.name: media
queries.shares: args {messageId, sha256, offset?}: the image's bytes as base64 (at most 180 KB raw per answer, from offset) with mime, width, height, total, length and done. Only an image attached to a message in this dashboard team's inbox whose attachment is cached on the Mac (never fetched for the viewer), at most 5 MB and a GIF, WebP, PNG or JPEG (never SVG). Also serves the picture face of the sender of a message in that inbox (a PNG drawn on the Mac, at most 96 px; the sha256 is the one the row's sender.face names), needing live.fields.inbox: [faces]. Attachments need live.fields.inbox: [media]. Anything else answers {refused: not_found | not_cached | too_large}. Reads mark nothing read

queries.describe: A story's linked sessions, tasks and complete cost/time totals
queries.name: storyChanges
queries.shares: args {storyId,limit?,cursor?,only?}; only (tasks, sessions, commits, prs, branches, worktrees, actual, reviews) answers just those arrays with totals, leaves the others out, and reads no git unless a git array is asked (without one totals.commits, files and lines are null with unavailable.commits, files and lines saying why, and a cursor is stale); reviews is the story's complete review rounds as {round,phase,scope,skill,subjectRev,high,medium,low,dismissed,converged,reportedAt} (no id, subject, reviewer, session or finding ids); paged commits projected to sha,authoredAt,repo-relative tracked files,sessionIds,basis (no subjects); branches to PR numbers, ref availability, merged SHA and basis only; worktrees to state and basis only; prs lists all observed merge/squash PR facts with source and basis (no branch names); planned/actual repo-relative file facts and decision numbers; all linked sessions projected to sessionId,basis,models,cost,timing; tasks projected to taskId,parentId,reviews. Complete totals, including totals.lines (counts of AI lines by runtime, human and unattributed lines over every commit, or null with an unavailable.lines reason), prs[].mergedAt (epoch ms), unavailable reasons and historyAsOf (fetchedAt, originHead). No account, record, absolute host paths, worktree paths, branch names, commit subjects, task goals, progress notes or idle gaps. No default row cap; an oversized answer fails rather than labelling partial rows complete

queries.describe: Many stories' complete cost/time/commit totals in one read, from the Mac's story totals index
queries.name: storyTotals
queries.shares: args {storyIds} (each passing the storyTotals.storyIds pin; a hosted ask holds the ids that fit the hosted 2 KB args limit (about 120 to 150), so pages call CS.storyTotals(ids), which asks in parts and merges one answer): {stories: {<id>: {totals (the storyChanges totals: counts, cost, time and lines counts), unavailable ({field: index into reasons}, only the reasons storyChanges publishes), computedAtMs, refreshing?, mergedAt (latest merge, epoch ms) or mergedAtReason, prs (newest 5 merged PRs as {number, merged}), prsTotal, runtimes (CLI ids), firstActivityAt and lastActivityAt (epoch ms over sessions' usage, commits, merges, tasks and review rounds; null with activityReason when none is recorded, or "refreshing" while an older row is recomputed), openSessions (sessions with observed timing and no end that were active in the 15 minutes before computedAtMs, by usage or turn; null while refreshing), linesInProgress (lines on story branches not merged yet, shaped like totals.lines; after a squash or rebase merge, lines stay here while the story's branch ref still exists, local or on origin, until it is deleted; null with linesInProgressReason)} | {pending: true} (not indexed yet, never zero) | {error: failed}}, reasons, pending (the pending ids), indexing {done, total}, truncated? and rest? (the ids left past 240 KB: ask again)}. Read from the index, never from git. No sessions, tasks, commits, files, paths, branch names or subjects

queries.describe: Committed line attribution and linked session facts from a local checkout
queries.name: whyLine
queries.shares: args {repo,rev?,story?,path,start,end}; repo,rev,revSource (explicit, mergedSha, branch or defaultBranch; an omitted rev never reads the checkout's HEAD),resolvedCommit,repo-relative path,notesRef (opaque snapshot id of the sense and ai notes refs),historyAsOf (fetchedAt, originHead),ranges projected to start,end,basis,commit,tool,model,sessionId,link,reason,story,candidateSessions,turn (sessionId,toolUseId,turn,basis,taskId,taskBasis,reason only),unavailable (turn only); sessions keyed by id with sessionId,basis,models,cost and allow-listed timing. Unavailable reads share status, reason and historyAsOf. No native session ids, records, accounts, host paths, commit subjects or conversation. Local objects only, never fetched

queries.describe: Whether line attribution and turn-link capture are working on this Mac
queries.name: setup
queries.shares: {attribution: {status: {kind, reason? (present only when the status is off; per-launch states appear on worktrees rows, not here)}, gitAiVersion, daemonReachable, supportedVersions, notesRef, capture: {lastSweepAt, trigger (startup|watcher), clonesSwept, logsSeen, logsNew, traceRowsStored, sessionMappingRowsStored, watchErrors, lastError}}}. Capture counts are since the app started (empty with lastSweepAt null until the first sweep); lastError is a fixed phase message. notesRef is the local notes ref (sense). Not the git-ai path, the previous-binary receipt, warnings, any status message text or the repos set to push notes.

queries.describe: Token use and spend per agent session on this Mac
queries.name: sessionUsage
queries.shares: per session: id, CLI, org, team, agent, models, first and last activity, message and token counts, cost; per day and in total: tokens and cost. Not the story each session was spent on (fields: story, its id, title, status and epic) or the working folder (fields: cwd). Newest activity first, at most 500 sessions, 50 by default. A cut list carries truncated, returned and total; days and totals still cover every session

queries.describe: The agent sessions CodeSense is running
queries.name: sessions
queries.shares: per session: handle, name, state, who launched it, story, role, agent, machine name, unread count, progress phase and step, deadline. Not the workspace (fields: workspace) or the progress note (fields: progressNote). In handle order, at most 500. A cut list carries truncated, returned and total

queries.describe: Recent agent runs and how each ended
queries.name: runs
queries.shares: {runs: [...]}, one row per run: story, run id, status, exit code, start and end times, how it ended, automation and trigger. Not the summary (fields: summary) or the workspace (fields: workspace). Newest first, at most 500, 50 by default. A cut list carries truncated, returned and total

queries.describe: Files in this dashboard's own team context (stories, epics, docs) by their metadata
fields: any frontmatter key except summary, relationships, body, text, path, content
queries.name: queryContext
queries.shares: per file in the one org and team whose context repo folder holds the dashboard folder (the org and team query_context lists for a file there), worked out when publish_dashboard runs only (never the private space): id, path inside the team, file name, kind, modified time, and only the frontmatter fields the dashboard lists (default: status, title, type, owner, updated). No file text, no summaries, no search, at most 500 rows. total and truncated are always present; a cut list also carries returned

available.describe: Recent dashboard actions and their progress
available.name: actions
available.shares: Last 50 calls: time, action, id, role, outcome, handle, run id and state; never email or prompts

available.describe: The workspaces open on this Mac in the dashboard's own team, pushed when they change
available.name: workspaces
