available.shares: {workspaces: [{id, name, story?, branch?, sessions: [handle], tabs}]}: per open workspace of the team whose context repo holds the dashboard folder: its id (an opaque key when the workspace id holds a folder path, so no local path is shared), its name (the story's title for a story workspace, else the folder's name for a folder workspace, else the id), the story id and its worktree branch when it has them, the handles of its watchable sessions and its tab count. Never other teams' workspaces or another machine's. Redacted

available.describe: The agent sessions running on this Mac in the dashboard's own team, pushed when they change
available.name: terminals
available.shares: {terminals: [row]}: per session with a live terminal on this Mac whose launch team is the dashboard's team: the sessions query's fields (handle, name, state, who launched it, story, role, avatar, agent, machine, unread, progress phase and step, deadline), workspace {id, name, story?, branch?} and watchable: true. Never sessions of another team, with no team or on another machine. Redacted

available.describe: One session's terminal, read-only: its screen and recent scrollback, then live output
available.name: terminal
available.shares: args {handle} (a handle from terminals): a snapshot of the most recent 2,000 lines (at most 1 MB, in parts with cols and rows), then the terminal's output, and resizes. The snapshot and the output are redacted (redaction recognises secrets by shape and labels, so it can't promise to hide every one). A handle that is unknown or not in the dashboard's team ends not_found; the session's exit ends exited. Watching never types or resizes

available.describe: The dashboard team's inbox, pushed on change without marking mail read
available.name: inbox
available.shares: The inbox query's projection, including text only with live.fields.inbox: [text], to/toName/replyTo/replyToName/contentType only with [meta], image attachments (hash and size only) only with [media], reactions [{emoji, count, mine}] only with [reactions] and sender.face only with [faces]. Same strict args (including scope human) and team scope; redacted. Re-read while watched using the shared list poller

available.name: tick

available.describe: Test stream: a counter value on a timer
available.name: tickValue

streams.declare: List the streams the page uses in dashboard.yml: `live: {streams: [name]}` (queries may be left out then). Only declared streams open; any other ends with not_declared. At most 16 names.
streams.limits: Each stream sends at most 256 KB a second and one frame per 50 ms; no data or vt part is over 64 KB; a value may be up to 256 KB as JSON and a snapshot up to 1 MB; a larger one ends the watch too_large. A viewer more than 1 MB behind gets gap. Between snapshots, seq only grows for data and value frames: a page can ignore one whose seq it has seen. Always apply a snapshot (one asked for with resync, or sent after a reconnect, may repeat a seq) and start afresh from it: the frames after it may repeat seqs seen before it.

page_api.ack: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'ack', wid, seq} is accepted and ignored: the shell acknowledges for the page
page_api.control: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'control', wid, on, reason?}: from the viewer only, when control of this watch turns on or off (reason: released, hidden, unwatched, switched, idle, replaced, reopened, access_ended, control_off, not_declared, ended, closed, mac_offline). A take the viewer sends can be refused with not_owner, control_off, mac_offline, not_ready (the terminal is still opening) or bad_request (not a terminal watch). A page cannot take control: a page that posts op control itself gets {op:'error', about:'control', source:'page', error} with not_owner for an invited viewer, control_off when the dashboard does not allow control, else bad_request
page_api.data: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'data', wid, seq, data}: output after the snapshot, in seq order
page_api.ended: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'ended', wid, reason:'exited'|'closed'|'not_found'|'not_declared'|'no_team'|'invalid_args'|'too_large'|'busy'|'failed'|'access_ended'|'replaced'}: the watch is over (no_team: the dashboard folder is in no team's context repo, so the agent streams have no team; closed: also sent by the shell after 8 refused or at-once-closed connections in a row, not counting a server going away or restarting; failed: the stream could not be opened or broke on the Mac, or this Mac never answered the open; access_ended: the viewer shows the request form; replaced: this viewer opened the dashboard in another window, so this window watches nothing more until it is reloaded)
page_api.error: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'error', wid, error:'rate_limited'|'bad_request'|'too_large'}: the watch is gone (except bad_request for a wid already watching, whose open watch goes on). rate_limited refuses this watch when the page has 8 watches already or the viewer made 240 watch and resync requests in the last minute (across reconnects; a refused resync ends its watch); only when the publishing Mac's 50 streaming connections (across its dashboards) are in use, or this viewer reconnects too often, does every open watch get it, with new watches refused for 30 s
page_api.gap: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'gap', wid}: this viewer fell behind and frames were dropped; send resync
page_api.hello: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'hello', role:'viewer'|'owner', control}: sent by the viewer to each page when it is shown; control is true only for the owner of a dashboard whose manifest allows control (taking it still needs the viewer's Take control button)
page_api.input: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'input', wid, kind:'keys'|'paste', data} or {cs:'live', v:1, op:'input', wid, kind:'resize', cols, rows}: owner only, and only for the watch under control. Refused with {op:'error', wid, error, about:'input'} (not_owner, not_controlling, control_off, too_large, rate_limited, mac_offline, refused, failed, bad_request); such an error does not end the watch
page_api.paused: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'paused', wid, reason:'mac_offline'|'reconnecting'}: frames resume, after watching, without any action
page_api.presence: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'presence', wid, watchers, controlling, mine}: how many watches of this stream are open, one per page watch (a viewer watching it twice counts twice); controlling is true while the owner controls this terminal, and mine is true for the watch in control
page_api.resized: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'resized', wid, seq, cols, rows}: a terminal's new size (terminal stream)
page_api.resync: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'resync', wid} after a gap: a fresh snapshot (a value stream: its current value) follows. It counts against the per-minute watch limit; past it, error rate_limited ends the watch
page_api.snapshot: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'snapshot', wid, seq, part, last, vt, cols?, rows?}: cols and rows come as a pair of 1..65535 or not at all; collect the parts, and replace what is shown with them joined once last is true; a part 0 starts a new snapshot and drops any parts collected so far
page_api.unwatch: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'unwatch', wid, pause?}: pause: true (the page went to the background) keeps the stream open at codesense.ai for up to 45 s, so a watch with from_seq on return gets the missed frames from its tail with no new snapshot; later, or without pause, the stream stops
page_api.viewport: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'viewport', covered}: from the viewer while the owner controls a terminal, how many CSS pixels at the bottom of the page a phone's on-screen keyboard covers (the toolkit's key bar stays above it); a page may ignore it
page_api.watch: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'watch', wid, stream, args, from_seq?} (at most 8 watches per page, more get error rate_limited; wid is the page's own id, a 1-100 character string or a number; args are a plain object of at most 2 KB as JSON (larger gets error too_large); a watch for a wid already watching gets error bad_request and the open watch goes on; from_seq is optional and inclusive (the frame with that seq comes again): the shell resumes each watch itself after a reconnect. seq values are large and grow across re-opens too; use them only to order frames, and start afresh at each snapshot (see limits). Every watch request counts against the per-minute limit, refused or not)
page_api.watching: {cs:'live', v:1, op:'watching', wid}: the stream is open (again, after paused)

streams.what: Streams push frames to the page as they happen, instead of asking again. The shell holds one WebSocket to the dashboard's own host per open dashboard; the page uses postMessage only, as for queries. A `value` stream sends the whole value on each change; a `bytes` stream sends a snapshot (one or more parts) and then ordered output. Every invited viewer can watch, up to 50 streaming connections at once across all the dashboards one Mac publishes (one per viewer session or owner sign-in per open dashboard; one more gets rate_limited).

api.CS.act(name, args): a promise of the result of one declared owner action; args contain only id and a declared choice. Never retries. Rejection is an error code; a timeout can still complete, so inspect activity before retrying
api.CS.confirmHint(): a promise that resolves once the hint is sent, with nothing about eligibility. Asks the viewer to show its own Confirm it's you pill when this browser's signed-in account is the dashboard owner's; it never opens the sheet and shows nothing to anyone else, so call it where the page would offer owner powers and design the page to work without the pill. Rejects no_shell outside the hosted viewer
api.CS.endOwnerAccess(): owner only: ends this browser's owner access on the server (the same path as the End owner access button), then the page reloads as a viewer. Call it from a click; rejects not_owner, needs_gesture, busy, failed, timeout
api.CS.fontRange: {min: 6, max: 18, initial: 13}, the terminal text sizes watchTerminal takes
api.CS.inbox(cb): cb(messages, state, detail) from the team inbox stream; returns stop(). Default message fields: messageId, from, fromName, summary, kind, createdAt (epoch ms), unread, inReplyTo, delivery.state when present. Text requires live.fields.inbox: [text]; to, toName, replyTo?, replyToName? and contentType (plain, markdown, html or null) require [meta]; attachments [{kind: image, alt, state, mime?, sha256?, width?, height?, bytes?}] require [media]; reactions [{emoji, count, mine}] (mine: the human reacted; never who reacted) require [reactions]. sender.face on a row requires [faces]: {sha256, mime: image/png, width, height} for a picture (pass its sha256 and the row's messageId to CS.media), {emoji} or {colour} (#rrggbb, the page draws the sender's initials on it); an agent with no face of its own is dealt one the way the in-app agents list deals it; the human has one only if they set it, and a sender whose face this Mac cannot resolve has none (show initials). Only for senders of the rows returned, never a roster. Reading never marks mail read. Query inbox takes only scope (to-human, to-agents, all, or human: only messages to or from the human, filtered on the Mac so no agent-to-agent mail leaves it), agentId, sessionId, role, limit; team is fixed by the dashboard. At most 500 messages, redacted.
api.CS.listAgents(cb): cb(rows, state, detail) from the terminals stream (detail: the end or error reason); returns stop()
api.CS.listWorkspaces(cb): cb(workspaces, state, detail) from the workspaces stream; returns stop()
api.CS.markRead(messageIds): Owner only: invokes ownerMarkRead through CS.act, as opening those messages in the app does. messageIds is 1 to 200 positive integer ids, each a message to the human in this team's inbox; one that is not (another team's, an agent's, a missing one) refuses the whole call with not_found and marks nothing. Resolves with {marked}, how many changed (already-read mail is left alone, so repeating a call resolves {marked: 0}). Rejects not_allowed (viewer), invalid_args, not_found or rate_limited (the relay's 10 acts a minute shared with sends and reactions, and 600 calls an hour on the Mac). The inbox stream pushes the new unread flags and humanUnread to every watcher.
api.CS.media(messageId, sha256): a promise of {url, mime, bytes} for one cached image of a message in this team inbox (an attachment with state cached, from live.fields.inbox: [media]; or the picture face of that message's sender, sha256 from the row's sender.face, from live.fields.inbox: [faces]; also list the media query in live.queries). url is a data: URL (base64), usable as an img src in the frame; nothing to revoke. The Mac only reads its cache (never fetches for a viewer); an image is read in chunks of at most 180 KB raw, one at a time, and one image at a time, backing off on rate_limited (60 asks a minute). Rejects not_approved (the media query, or media and faces both missing from live.fields.inbox, is not declared; the relay's query_not_declared), not_found (not this team's message or hash, and for a face not the face of that message's sender: the same answer for every miss), not_cached (pending, blocked, failed or evicted) or too_large (over 2 MB: show a card instead). api.CS.onActions(cb): cb(rows, state, detail) from the actions stream (last 50 calls, with session or routine progress); returns stop()
api.CS.onControl(cb): cb({handle, on, reason}) when control of a terminal turns on or off (reason as in the control message: closed when the connection drops, mac_offline when the Mac goes away; or, from the toolkit itself, hidden when the page goes to the background, ended when the terminal ends or fails, unwatched on dispose), and cb({handle, on, error, lost}) when an input was refused (any input error: rate_limited, too_large, mac_offline, refused, failed, not_controlling, control_off, bad_request; too_large also when a paste or the queue would pass 1 MB; on says whether control is still on, lost that queued input was dropped), and cb({handle, on: false, error, about: 'control'}) when a take was refused, and cb({handle, on, lost: true, interrupted: true}) when the owner's own Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D, Ctrl-Z or Esc dropped what was still waiting (it is sent at once); returns stop()
api.CS.onPresence(cb): cb({mac, mac_seen_at}) for the owner's Mac, or cb({wid, watchers, controlling, mine}) for a watched stream; test which shape arrived before reading its fields. wid identifies the page watch. Returns stop()
api.CS.partialList(opts): CS.partialList({container,render,subscribe:cb=>CS.subscribeAll(...,cb,{manual:true}),onResult?}) -> {el,loadMore(),refresh(),stop()}. Binds the real subscription handle, controls loading/unknown/zero/complete/ceiling/error/Retry, prevents double clicks and handles Promise failures. Existing-layout binding: {status:element,button:element,subscribe,onResult}; no extra row list. Optional query:()=>queryAll(...) supports a one-time list. Legacy loadMore callback remains supported. One handle per resource/scope; stop the old component before scope change or rebinding status/button. Wrap results in your resource store run(resource,scope,fn); its slot owns value/error/token/scope, the handle owns pages. Stop on pagehide/teardown.
api.CS.passing(reason): true for an end or error that passes (closed, failed, busy, rate_limited): such a watch opens again by itself when the page is next shown, and watchTerminal also opens its terminal again after 15 s (then longer, up to 2 min); a page that retries a CS.watch sooner calls the old watch's stop() first, or both would open
api.CS.query(name, args): one live answer (a query frame). busy/mac_busy (every Mac slot taken) and rate_limited (every relay slot taken) are asked again after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 8 s before the error is the page's
api.CS.queryAll(name, args, opts?): CS.queryAll(name,args,opts?) -> Promise<{rows,total,returned,complete,truncated,loading,error,canLoadMore,atCeiling,...}> for sessionUsage, queryContext, storyChanges (commits by sha; sessions metadata retained). opts override shapes: rows key path or answer=>array, id key or row=>id, cursor:{arg,next} with next key path or answer=>cursor|null, total key path or answer=>number. Undefined options keep defaults; cursor arg/next merge individually. Unknown verbs page only with opts.rows; otherwise single-answer behavior. Captures filters and effective limit (default100); sequential pages, hard maxRows5000, up to 3 silent walks from the head on stale_cursor (only the new walk replaces rows), one other stale restart and <=2 full same-limit recovery walks. Complete only when known numeric total equals distinct loaded rows and no cursor. Unknown/overshoot stay partial; zero can be complete. Latest total/totals/days replace, never sum. Explicit page asks back off5s*n up to6 retries; ordinary errors reject. Usage identity exact(cli,sessionId); machineId metadata. No snapshot guarantee. Actual outer source/answered_at/server_time metadata is preserved when provided.
api.CS.react(messageId, emoji, remove?): Owner only: invokes ownerReact through CS.act. emoji is one of 😂 ❤️ 👍 😮 🎉 🔥 and messageId a positive id of a message in this team inbox. Without remove it toggles; remove true takes the reaction back, false makes sure it is there. Resolves with {on} (the reaction is on now). Rejects not_allowed (viewer), invalid_args (other emoji), not_found (not this team's message) or rate_limited (120 an hour). Shows in CS.inbox as reactions only with live.fields.inbox: [reactions]; a reaction is not unread mail or a reply.
api.CS.ready(): a promise of {role, control} once the viewer says hello; rejects no_shell after 3 s, as in the CodeSense viewer on the Mac, where no live data comes
api.CS.resize(handle, cols, rows): a promise: asks that session for this size (1-1000 columns, 1-500 rows), under the same rules (not_controlling, too_large when the queue is full); the owner's Mac pane takes its size back when it is used
api.CS.role(): viewer or owner (null before the hello)
api.CS.send(to, text, replyTo?): Owner only: invokes ownerMessage through CS.act. Recipient is human, role:<id>, or a running local session handle in the dashboard team. Plain text only, 1 to 2,000 characters, at most 60 sends/hour. replyTo is a positive messageId shown in this team inbox; replies follow its Reply-To within the team. No attachments, HTML format or click actions. Resolves with status and messageId; never auto-retry a send with an unknown outcome. Message bodies are never logged.
api.CS.sendInput(handle, text, opts): a promise that resolves once the text is sent to that terminal, or queued behind a paste still being sent (a later refusal, or control ending while it waited, comes through onControl with lost: true); opts {paste: true} sends it as a paste. Rejects not_controlling unless the owner has taken control of it with the viewer's own Take control button (a page cannot take control itself), and too_large over 16 KB or when 1 MB or 1600 messages already wait to be sent; input goes in order
api.CS.storyTotals(ids): CS.storyTotals(ids) -> Promise<{stories, reasons, pending, indexing, source, answered_at?}> for any number of story ids: asks storyTotals in parts that fit the hosted 2 KB args limit (about 120 to 150 ids), three at a time, asks again for any rest, and merges one answer (reason indexes renumbered into one reasons list; source cache and the oldest answered_at when any part came from the cache). Needs storyTotals declared and pinned like storyChanges.
api.CS.subscribeAll(name, args, everyS, cb,: CS.subscribeAll(name,args,everyS,cb,opts?) -> callable stop with Promise-returning stop.loadMore()/refresh(). opts.manual:true makes each loadMore fetch one next page; default auto-walks. Identical cached head bodies preserve newer page rows/summary. Only a successful complete fresh traversal replaces membership. Live errors in result.error retain rows/cursor. Stop settles own lifecycle promises, clears own backoff and subscriptions; dispatched transport may finish. Server-owned head rate_limited errors are visible until next >=15s tick; explicit page backoff is separate.
api.CS.viewer(cb): cb({role: owner|viewer, mac: online|offline|unknown|null, mac_seen_at, updated_at, stale, display}) now and on each change; display is the signed-in viewer's own email, or owner; subscribing also tells the viewer this page shows offline and stale itself (chrome: none). api.CS.watch(stream, args, handlers): one stream watch: handlers {state(s, detail), value, snapshot(vt, cols, rows), data, resized(cols, rows), presence(watchers, controlling)}; resyncs after a gap; returns {stop()}
api.CS.watchTerminal(handle, element, opts): an xterm.js terminal in element at the session's own size, scrolling inside the element and following new output until the viewer scrolls up, and opening itself again after a passing end (no page retry needed). Read-only, except for the owner while they control it (see control): then it takes keys, and on a phone (or with opts.keyBar true) shows a key bar with Esc, Tab, a sticky Ctrl, the arrows and a line field whose Enter sends the line and Enter. opts {fontSize} (6 to 18, default 13), {fit} (default true: fits the font to the width, capped at 18px, without resizing the PTY; spare rows show scrollback), {theme} (github-dark by default; also dracula, nord, catppuccin, solarized-dark), {keyBar} (true or false to force the bar); returns {dispose(), onState(cb), onFollow(cb), onResize(cb), onControl(cb), controlling(), onFit(cb), setFontSize(px), fontSize(), setFit(on), fitting(), jumpToLatest(), size()}; setFontSize turns fit off, setFit(true) restores it, onFit calls cb({fontSize, fit}) when either changes

toolkit.control: Owner control: only the dashboard's owner, signed in to codesense.ai with a passkey or password and a second factor, on a dashboard whose dashboard.yml says `live: {streams: [terminal, ...], control: owner}`, can type into a terminal. The owner clicks Take control in the viewer's top bar (outside the page; it acts on the page's newest terminal watch), and the viewer shows a bar saying which session they control, with Release. Control ends on Release, a page change, the page going to the background, the owner's Mac going offline, 10 minutes with no typing (a resize does not count), another window or dashboard of the owner taking it, the dashboard no longer allowing control, the session ending or no longer being shared, the connection dropping, and when the owner's access ends (their owner sign-in for this dashboard ending or expiring, or the dashboard unpublished). Invited viewers never type, by any path: the viewer, codesense.ai and the Mac each refuse it. Input is at most 16 KB per message and 64 KB and 100 messages a second; a paste typed into the terminal (up to 1 MB) is sent in pieces of at most 12 KB within those limits, each a paste of its own (cut at a line break where one is near; the Mac brackets each piece that has a line break). What is typed is never logged; who controlled which session, when, and how many messages and bytes are.
toolkit.phone: Watches stop while the page is hidden (visibilitychange) and resume with from_seq when it is shown, so missed output arrives without a redraw when the viewer still holds it, else as a fresh snapshot. Only the watches a page opens stream: open one terminal at a time.
toolkit.reserved: CS.launch and CS.stop are names kept for later
toolkit.states: connecting, live, paused (mac_offline, reconnecting, or hidden while the page is in the background), ended (with the reason), error (with the code). An end or error with a passing reason (CS.passing) opens again when the page is next shown; any other end or error is final
toolkit.what: cs-live.js (the helper above, version comment `// cs-live 4`) wraps the page API in plain functions on one global, CS. It is a convenience: a page that posts the messages itself works the same. create_dashboard {template: "workspaces"} or {template: "mission-control"} writes it with xterm.js 6.0.0 (vendor/xterm.js, vendor/xterm.css) and lists them. Both templates default to view-only; add control: true to write live.control: owner (only the owner may type, after Take control in the shell). Mission control declares queries [inbox, sessions], streams [inbox, terminals, terminal], and fields.inbox [text], with agents ordered by attention, a role line and a team inbox; Workspaces groups sessions by their open workspaces. Leave pages, data and live out for either template. To use it in another dashboard, copy those three files into the folder and list them in publish.files. Load vendor/xterm.js before cs-live.js.

hosted.what: A dashboard published to codesense.ai can ask the owner's Mac live, read-only queries while the Mac is connected. The page posts each request to its own window with postMessage(msg, '*') (not parent.postMessage); the frame forwards it to the shell, which relays through codesense.ai to the Mac and back.

agents_and_inbox.inbox: await codesense.inbox({scope?, agentId?, sessionId?, role?, kind?, conversation?, before?, limit?}) [inbox_list] → {messages: [{messageId, conversation, from, fromName, to, toName, text, createdAtMs, inReplyTo, inReplyToTeam, toHuman, unread, primaryFile?, attachments, archivedAtMs?, delivery, onClick?, contentType?, replyTo?, replyToName?, summary?, replyTargetEnded, via?, reactions: [{emoji, count, reactors: [handle|'human']}], kind}], humanUnread, conversations: [{with, team, unread, messageCount, lastAt, lastMessageId, lastPreview}], hasMore}. Newest first, at most 500 rows initially. conversations covers all human conversation history; unread excludes archived/read mail. conversation filters by a summary with key, before is a positive message id (exclusive); ask for limit:50 to page a conversation, including replies whose roots are outside the payload. hasMore stays true until its oldest page is returned. In a cross-team view pass {org,team} per request and merge pages by team and messageId. kind: needs-you (waits on the human) | update (informational) — terminal-typed rows are update; else the sender's kind; else needs-you when it carries a replyTo naming someone other than the human, its sender or a role its sender holds; else update (kind describes mail to the human for agent views and dashboards). Pass kind to list only that kind (applied before limit). Both kinds appear as conversations in the human Inbox; all unread human mail counts in its badge. humanUnread counts both kinds. scope: to-human | to-agents | all (default to-human with no filter, all with one). agentId: a saved Agent's role inbox + its running instances' inboxes + replies; sessionId: one session's sent and received mail; role: one role queue. delivery (role messages): {state: queued|reading|accepted|done|withdrawn, pickedUpAtMs, instance, acceptedAtMs, disposition, note, withdrawnAtMs}. replyTo (when the sender set one): where replies go instead of the sender — a session handle, human, or role:<id>; replyTargetEnded: a reply would land in a session that is no longer running. summary (when the sender set one): a one-line plain-text gist — show it in list rows instead of text. Render text by contentType (markdown default) with textContent or a sanitizer, never raw innerHTML.
agents_and_inbox.inboxRollup: await codesense.inboxRollup() → {messages, conversations, roles}, the list_inbox_rollup DTO. conversations carries {with, team, unread, messageCount, lastAt, lastMessageId, lastPreview} over all history per team; page older conversation mail using inbox({org,team,conversation:with,before,limit:50}). Every synced team's messages (human, session and role recipients), agent notes and role queues. Messages use {id, conversation, team: {org, team}, from, fromName, to, toName, toRole, text, contentType, createdAtMs, inReplyTo, via, replyTo, summary, unread, delivery, kind, attachments}; unlike inbox(), the id field is id, not messageId. to is a session handle or human, or null for a role queue named by toRole. unread is relative to the recipient; filter to === human for the human inbox. Ids are unique only within team: key by org, team and id. Updates also carry team: {org, team}; roles are merged by role name. Requires inbox:read:all-teams in the Rust frame grant. The default open policy grants it to every dashboard, including team panes; team-safe limits it to declared private and built-in dashboards unless explicitly overridden. Re-read on onInboxChanged for mail, onAgentsChanged for role changes, and window message codesense:agent-activity-changed for agent notes. These events cover every team. A missing capability rejects with 'denied: grant'.
agents_and_inbox.live: const off = codesense.onAgentsChanged(() => reread()) follows versioned agentDefinitions rows when saved definitions or running counts change, plus compatibility revisions for role registrations, queues and the human's status; codesense.onInboxChanged((change?) => …) when a message is stored, read, claimed or reacted to (change.changes, when present: [{team: {org, team}, messageIds}] names the messages the committed update re-read, only your team's when you are team-scoped; re-read just those); window message `codesense:agent-activity-changed` when an update is posted. Each returns an unsubscribe. Re-read with the calls above. Registrations and claims also lapse with time, so a queue view may re-read on a slow timer (e.g. every 30s while visible).
agents_and_inbox.media_messages: inbox() and inboxRollup() image attachments carry {kind:'image', sha256?, mime?, width?, height?, bytes?, alt, sourceUrl?, sourceHost?, state:'cached'|'pending'|'blocked'|'failed', reason?, retryable}. Render cached bytes from same-origin /media/v1/<sha256>, never from sourceUrl. Pending or retryable failed rows can call act('loadMedia', {org?,team?,messageId}) after the person taps. Blocked means remote media is off in team config; offer a source link, not a fetch. Respect OS Reduce Motion with a still first frame and explicit play/pause.
agents_and_inbox.role: One read model for agents and their inboxes. Every call returns the same shape as its MCP twin (named in brackets), so a dashboard and an agent see the same data. Team-scoped calls act on the page's own team (else the active team). Reads mark nothing read and claim nothing.
agents_and_inbox.roles: await codesense.roles({role?, limit?}) [role_state] → {roles: [{role, roleName, registrations: [{instanceId, instanceName, generation, registeredAtMs, lastRenewedAtMs, expiresAtMs, live}], counts: {pending, claimed, accepted, acknowledged}, deliveries: [{deliveryId, messageId, state, from, fromName, excerpt, createdAtMs, firstClaimedAtMs, claimOwner, claimOwnerName, claimOwnerGeneration, claimExpiresAtMs, claimLapsed, receipt}], deliveriesTruncated}]}. Delivery state: pending (nobody holds it) | claimed (an instance is deciding; claimLapsed = its claim expired) | accepted (as work or no_work, not yet acknowledged) | acknowledged (finished). Open deliveries are all listed; `limit` caps acknowledged ones per role (default 20). A registration's `live` turns false at expiresAtMs.
agents_and_inbox.sample: content/examples/dashboards/agent-inbox-console.html in the CodeSense docs context repo (getting-started team) shows sessions, role queues and the human inbox live, with reply and mark-read.
agents_and_inbox.updates: await codesense.updates({limit?}) [list_agent_updates] → {updates: [{id, sessionId, agentName, role, text, createdAtMs}]} — agents' progress notes, newest first. These notes are available to dashboards and do not appear in the native human Inbox. Read update mail sent to the human with inbox({kind:'update'}).

context_query.docs: Same model as the `query_context` MCP tool — see its description for every operator.
context_query.epics: A row's relationships.parentEpic is the parent_epic/epic frontmatter; relationships.folderEpic is the nearest folder holding a README/index (the epic as the left nav shows it). Ask for both with select: [..., 'relationships'].
context_query.live: const off = codesense.subscribeContext(q, (result, err) => render(result)) — runs now and again on every context change; call off() to stop.
context_query.own_team: const {org, team, layer, contentRoot} = await codesense.context() — where this page lives (null outside every content root; team is null in the private space). Scope a query to the page's own team with where: {orgs: [org], teams: [team], layers: ['team']}, or to its own content root with where: {sameRootAs: contentRoot + '/x'}.
context_query.paging: Pass nextCursor back as q.cursor with the same query. A walk's pages read one index snapshot, kept 30 s after each page and 120 s after its first page at most (4 snapshots at most); a text query's walk pages only until the index changes. Past that, or after an app restart, the call rejects with a message starting stale_cursor: restart without a cursor (kit.queryAll and kit.subscribeAll do it silently). A cursor from another query rejects with invalid cursor.
context_query.scope: Team content is footprint-wide (every synced org) unless q.where.orgs / q.where.sameOrgAs narrows it. Private-space items only ever come from the page's own org, whatever the query asks; all-orgs files match every org.

frame_presentation.builtins: builtin:stop, builtin:close-tab and builtin:set-role use host labels, icons, availability and handlers. Stop and Close tab always use the host confirmation. Results include builtin:true after the action settles. Unknown builtin ids reject, including builtin:relaunch.
frame_presentation.commands: A slot dashboard (right-pane, dock or file-nav) declares commands in its pane-manifest.yaml entry or a <meta name="codesense:commands"> JSON array: [{id, label, icon?, defaultChord?, scope: global|slot-visible|slot-focused, humanOnly?}]. The host owns their chords (rebindable in Settings, conflicts resolved there), lists them in the command palette, and delivers each run as codesense.onCommand(({id, args, dispatchId}) => …), once per dispatchId and only after the page's ready(); a closed slot is revealed first. codesense.commands.register(ids) sets which declared commands are active now (the last call replaces the set; an undeclared id is refused). codesense.commands.list() and codesense.commands.run(id, args) are the page's twins of the MCP tools command_list and command_run and need commands:run. Agents can't run humanOnly commands; the person can switch humanOnly per command or per dashboard in Settings, and team-safe locks it on for private dashboards.
frame_presentation.default_menu: Architecture: put JSON in data-codesense-row: {kind:'story'|'epic'|'file', path} (team-content-relative; epic path names the folder), {kind:'agent', sessionId} or {kind:'agent', agentId}, {kind:'workspace', workspaceId}, or {kind:'group', groupId}. Nav paths resolve only against the active team's mounted nav tree; workspace/group ids resolve through its native workspace tray. Architecture: inbox tags are {kind:'conversation', key, conversations:[{with,team}]}, {kind:'message', messageId, team?}, {kind:'attachment', path, team?}, {kind:'role-queue', role, key?, team?, conversations?}. Inbox builders resolve stored messages through existing granted reads; attachment paths retain their team. Every menu reuses the native builder and handlers. Architecture: register codesense.onMenuAction(({itemId,row}) => ...) for page-local Open/Reply/Open queue/New message. Without a listener the host omits those items. Hosted HTML messages use their stored message/team and the inbox parent callback; fields and selection still take precedence. Mark as unread notifies the page before its write, holding the conversation until explicit Open/Reply/Jump to latest. Policy: Copy link is excluded until messages have an openable link. Policy: automatic text, nav and dashboard menus need no sessions:read grant; the agent menu stays gated. Unknown/unresolved tags or denied agent menus fall back to the dashboard menu. Architecture: fields or selected text at the pointer get the shared Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All menu before any row tag. The shim always suppresses the browser menu, including baseline and hosted frames. Baselines show text menus only; hosted children present through their parent. A page's preventDefault or showMenu wins in the event task or the one-tick defer. One menu at a time; reload/unmount closes it and focus returns only to a connected frame. Text edits restore the exact field and selection, including fields with no id. Architecture: readonly codesense.textMenuOpen is true only while the host holds the frame's automatic text menu; blur handlers defer only while it is true, and lifecycle onFlush must save pending field edits before teardown. Paste reads the clipboard only after a person activates Paste. Policy: empty space gets builtin:reload-pane, builtin:open-as-tab (slots only), builtin:edit-source (editable sources only); centre tabs say Reload tab.

file_drop.delivery: Architecture: native file drags reach only the topmost iframe under the native event position, when it is a visible, ready local pane slot (right-pane, dock or file-nav). The host sends leave on exiting that frame, cancellation/drag end, hiding or teardown. Published pages, nested message frames, centre tabs and baseline viewers do not receive these messages. Listen on window and require event.source === parent. Named types: CodesenseSdk.FileDragMessage and CodesenseSdk.FileDropMessage. This is a host push, with no Surface SDK method or bridge verb.
file_drop.drop: {type:'codesense:file-drop', paths:string[]} — absolute OS paths only on actual drop.
file_drop.grant: Policy: reuse the existing files:read grant. The open preset includes it; team-safe panes must declare files:read. A person's explicit drop authorizes disclosure of those paths to that eligible pane only. There is no new capability, filesystem read permission or confinement change.
file_drop.handling: The page decides what to do with a drop. The host does not ingest files or change a composer automatically. Drag enter/over/leave carry no paths; only an actual drop discloses paths.

frame_presentation.focus: codesense.focusOut({direction}) returns to the previous host element or terminal; codesense.focusTerminal() focuses the active workspace terminal. Both pass through frame admission and have no MCP twin.
frame_presentation.focus_return: When the host UI closes, the host focuses the iframe and sends codesense:focus-return {anchorId}. The shim focuses that id, else its first focusable control. codesense.onFocusReturn(cb) passes {anchorId} and returns an unsubscribe; any registered handler replaces default focus.
frame_presentation.menus: await codesense.showMenu({anchorRect, anchorId, row, items}) renders in the host. Rectangles are frame-relative. Returns {itemId, row} or {closed:true}; a second request closes the first.
frame_presentation.popovers: await codesense.showPopover({kind:'agent-quick-send', sessionId, anchorRect, anchorId}) uses the host quick-send popup; kind 'agent-inbox-chat' opens the agent's inbox chat. Both resolve {closed:true}. Unknown kinds reject.

sdk.has: codesense.has(name) → true when name is one of these features or a verb this frame's effective grant admits (no feature is a verb name); false until the host answers the shim's ready. Informational only: Rust still checks every call. Under the default open preset every verb reports true. Types for every verb and the SDK surface: /kit/v1/codesense.d.ts.
sdk.intent: const off = codesense.onIntent((intent) => …) — receives the opaque JSON object (at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes) supplied to pane_open. Returns an unsubscribe. The host posts {type:'codesense:intent', intent} when ready, or after codesense:ready on a new/reloaded document. One pending intent per panel, newest wins; delivered intents are cleared and never replayed after reload. The shim buffers the last undelivered intent for a late subscriber and consumes it once. The page interprets it; the host does not.

live_hub.files: Use codesense.files.list({scope:'team'|'private'|'story'|'agent',team?,storyId?,agentId?,dir?}) for {rows:[{id,path,name,kind:'dir'|'file'|'story'|'epic',size?,mtime?}]}. Story uses hydrate_story's default file closure; agentId is the full agent key and uses its context want set. Own content only until the sharing gate is connected; private scope is your private space. Read with files.read({path,maxBytes?}) for {text?,bytesUrl?,size,truncated,sha256}; text is capped at 1.5 MB, with a /viewer URL for larger or binary files. files.create({path,content?,onCollision:'keep-both'|'fail'}) returns {path}; files.move({from,to}) returns {fromPath,toPath}; files.delete({path}) returns {deletedPath}. MCP twins: list_context_content (omit context and use scope), read_content_file, create_content_file, move_content_file, delete_content_file. Subscribe with codesense.subscribe('files',{scope,dir?,storyId?,agentId?,window:[0,200],onChange}); page with codesense.page('files',cursor,options). Views are grant-derived team:<key>|files:<selector>, fed by the existing context-file-change watcher; never poll. Declare slots: file-nav for one context-following sidebar body, with host-owned width/collapse/resize. The native PipelineStatusNav stays default. ui:file-nav holds per-team {expanded,selected?,scope?}; native and pane share the same expansion backing store. Teaching example: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/pane-shapes.html#file-nav.
live_hub.machineStats: Native Machines subscription: keyed by machine id (id), snapshot plus versioned deltas through this one hub. Resource fields match machines(): load1, cpuCount, memUsedBytes, memTotalBytes, diskFreeBytes, diskTotalBytes, diskPath, sampledAt and machineStatsSupported. The host watches only with subscribers; hidden/disposed frames and closed windows release subscriptions. Samples every 30 seconds while watched, no per-view polling; runtime state only.
live_hub.navLens: ui:file-nav mirrors the native viewer store in both directions: source {kind:'clone'|'private'} or {kind:'worktree',id}, view files|changes|history, lens everything|needs|agents|ready|active|review|blocked|not_started|done, arrange folders|stage, storiesOnly, doneOpen and historyBranches. setUiState writes the native setter; no independent persisted lens exists. files rows additionally expose starterPage, mergeMarked, shadows, overrides, installedSourceRepo, repoGlyph and repoTint from the native owners; installed groups keep their installed:// path. kit.stageRail(role,ready), kit.statusMark(mark) and kit.fileKindIcon(kind) are generated from native renders with matching metrics, colours and motion. showMenu items accept a kit icon name or {kind:'stageRail',role,ready}, {kind:'statusMark',mark}, {kind:'fileKindIcon',fileKind}; count, radioGroup with checked, and segmented:[{id,label,checked}] extend ordinary items. Choice returns the selected child itemId.
live_hub.notes_example: A private Notes page: const {rows} = await codesense.records.list({collection:'notes'}) (pinned first, then most recent); const note = await codesense.records.read({collection:'notes', id}); keep note.body as base and save with const r = await codesense.records.write({collection:'notes', id, body, base, requestId}); when r.merged is true show r.body and highlight r.overlaps. Pin with codesense.records.setFields({collection:'notes', id, fields:{pinned:true}}). codesense.records.delete({collection:'notes', id}) is confirmable and human-only (agents can't delete notes); bring a note back with codesense.records.restore({collection:'notes', id, commit}) using a commit from records.history.
live_hub.records: Use codesense.records.collections/list/read/search/history/readAt/create/write/setFields/delete/restore. Every call takes collection; scope, org, team and profile are bound to the frame. Subscribe with codesense.subscribe('records', {collection, window?: [from,to], onChange}); records views default to 200 rows, contain no bodies, and page through codesense.page('records', cursor, {collection}). Multiple collection subscriptions are independent; unsubscribe with its callback or {collection} as the third argument. The view key is records:<scope>:<org>[/<team>]:<collection>. Writer deltas carry actor, kind and optional requestId; duplicate requests and unchanged index rows produce no delta. Private history commits later update headCommit only. Team and story collections have no automatic history.
live_hub.sessions: codesense.onSessions(cb) is subscribe('sessions')-backed. The Rust projection is shared by native and MCP consumers. Inbox and agentList projections are available through subscribe. onAgentsChanged follows the agentDefinitions projection, including unused saved agents changed by a save, external edit or pull; agents() reads its cached summary rows. Rich agent({key}) remains a fresh canonical read of resolved startup and login state. Compatibility revisions preserve role and human-status notifications. onInboxChanged retains visible-only inbox invalidations. No per-frame session re-reads or hidden polling.
live_hub.stories: Subscribe to stories with {window:[0,200],onChange}; use page('stories',cursor) for more. This is a team-scoped, grant-derived team: view over the existing native full-team pipeline scan, taxonomy, dependency graph, agent marks and recursive epic counts. Rows are keyed by path; kind is story, epic, doc or main-doc. Stories carry storyId, declared title (without a repeated id), status, taxonomy role and label, ready, blockedBy, dependencyCount, mark, sprint, metadataValid and metadataInvalidReason. Epics carry total, done and a rolled-up mark. ownerPath locates docs and main docs. Null means absent. The existing watcher feeds snapshots plus deltas; never poll. Declare team scope or use the file-nav slot for a team-bound view.
live_hub.subscribe: await codesense.subscribe(topic, {sinceRev?, window?: [from,to], onChange?}) returns {topic, viewKey, rev, snapshot, total?, cursor?}; inbox snapshots contain at most 200 rows. codesense.page(topic,cursor) loads older rows. onChange(snapshot, delta) receives the updated rows after each codesense:delta {topic, viewKey, rev, baseRev?, upserts, removes, requestId?}. A burst may arrive as one delta with baseRev, the revision immediately before the folded changes. Row id is stable. Revisions are per filtered team/space view; a gap resyncs. Hidden frames receive one stale marker and do no reads; showing resyncs from the last revision. firstPaint uses the same snapshot shape.
live_hub.ui: Use ui:<slotId> for shared selection, folds and arrangement: subscribe then codesense.setUiState(topic, patch, requestId). Native and page share the host-owned state; writes persist separately from page-private prefs and echo requestId in the resulting delta.

sdk.liveness: Call `codesense.ready()` once your page has rendered; a pane that doesn't, and never subscribes, falls back after 3 s. The shim's automatic codesense:ready is a transport handshake only. An admitted page subscribe counts immediately, even when its snapshot waits for visibility. Denied calls do not count.

nav_selection.example: if (typeof codesense.onNavSelectionChange === 'function') codesense.onNavSelectionChange((sel) => { const id = sel && sel.file && sel.file.id; document.querySelectorAll('[data-story]').forEach((el) => el.classList.toggle('selected', el.dataset.story === id)); }); // feature-detect: older CodeSense has no nav selection
nav_selection.live: const off = codesense.onNavSelectionChange((sel) => …) — runs now (once known) and once per settled change (bursts are coalesced; an unchanged selection is not re-sent; a hidden page catches up when shown). Returns an unsubscribe. Selection arrives through the frame slot context. getNavSelection() resolves null rather than wait past 5 s. Event-driven: never poll it. Feature-detect both (typeof codesense.onNavSelectionChange === 'function') so the page still works on an older CodeSense.
nav_selection.read: await codesense.getNavSelection() → {org, team, file, drill} | null. file: {path (absolute), relPath, kind ('story'|'bug'|'spike'|'epic'|'doc'|… or null when not indexed), id (story id / epic id or null), title, epic (a story's parent epic, else its folder epic; an epic doc's own id)} | null. drill: {path, relPath, epic: {id, title, path, relPath} | null (the epic main doc in that folder or its nearest ancestor)} | null at the nav root.
nav_selection.reveal: To select or reveal a file in the nav, call codesense.openFile({path}) — it opens the file as the active tab and expands its folders. There is no separate select verb.
nav_selection.scope: Read-only: the host sends the selection in slot context after ready and on settled changes. The selection is always the page's own team: a right pane gets the team it is shown in, an HTML inbox message its message's team, a centre dashboard the team its file lives in. A path outside that team's content root (another team, a source repo) reads as null, never as its path.
nav_selection.what: What the left nav has selected — the open file and the folder the nav is drilled into — with the story or epic each one is. Use it to make a dashboard or right pane follow the nav (highlight the selected story, scope to the drilled epic).

pane_chrome.badge: codesense.setBadge({count, severity?: 'info'|'warning'|'error'}) shows a count on the panel's title bar, even while the section is collapsed; setBadge(null) or a count of 0 clears it. A reload clears it.
pane_chrome.icon: `<meta name="codesense:icon" content="git-pull-request">` — any Lucide icon name (kebab-case or PascalCase) for the panel tab; an unknown name shows a "?" glyph.
pane_chrome.title: The pane's `<title>` is its panel title.

sdk.prefs: if (codesense.prefs) { const p = await codesense.prefs(); … } → this dashboard's own settings object ({} at first); await codesense.setPrefs({details: 'compact'}) merges keys (null removes one) and resolves the result. Feature-detect both (an older CodeSense has neither: fall back to localStorage). Kept in the user's app state by DashboardRef identity; a private copy inherits installedFrom preferences until its first write, then keeps its own settings. Settings survive restarts; prefer it over localStorage, which a restart clears. 16 KB per dashboard.

routines_runs_and_machines.example: const off = codesense.onRoutinesChanged(render); render(); async function render() { const list = await codesense.routines(); for (const r of list) { const {runs} = await codesense.routineRuns({key: r.id, limit: 5}); /* draw r.name and runs[i].phase with textContent */ } }
routines_runs_and_machines.live: codesense.onRoutinesChanged(cb) (a routine or one of its runs changed), codesense.onMachinesChanged(cb) (a machine was saved, removed, shared or changed connection state), codesense.onWorktreesChanged(cb) (a managed worktree was added or removed) each run cb on the host's payloadless nudge (window messages codesense:routines-changed, codesense:machines-changed, codesense:worktrees-changed) and return an unsubscribe: re-read then. Session progress arrives with onSessions.
routines_runs_and_machines.machines: await codesense.machines() [list_machines with the page's org and team] → [{machineId ('local' = This Mac), kind (local|ssh), label, scope (null | {kind:'personal'} | {kind:'team', orgSlug, team}), declaration, binding, canPublish, status: {state: connected (with workspaces) | idle | connecting | handshaking | reconnecting | disconnected | unreachable | connectionFailed | needsCredential | authFailed | hostKeyChanged | notInstalled | versionMismatch | terminalServerFrozen, ...}, attention (agents there waiting on you), capabilities: {agentCallbacks}, terminalServer? (connected only: {serverVersion?, appVersion, upToDate, relation: same|older|newer|otherBuild, ...})}]. Also optional load1 (1-minute load average), cpuCount (logical cores), memUsedBytes (total minus available), memTotalBytes, diskFreeBytes, diskTotalBytes (all byte counts), diskPath (workspace volume path), sampledAt (server Unix epoch milliseconds), machineStatsSupported (false means unknown: update the terminal server). Resource values are self-reported runtime observations, never synced or reservations. MCP uses a sample under 30 seconds old or one one-shot sample; a read does not subscribe. The native Machines tab watches the machineStats topic while visible, using snapshot plus deltas every 30 seconds. This Mac first, then the team's shared machines, then your private ones.
routines_runs_and_machines.model_rates: await codesense.modelRates() [model_rates] → [{modelPrefix, effectiveFrom (YYYY-MM-DD; 1970-01-01 for a seeded list price), inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok (null: 0.1x input), long ({fromTokens, inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok (null: 0.1x the long input price)} or null: one price at every prompt length), source ('set by the user' after native acceptance, 'set by an agent' for effective MCP/page requests, or the seeded list price's note)}], every stored rate (USD per million tokens), by model prefix and then by day. A model's rate on a day is the latest one from on or before that day, under its longest matching prefix. act('setModelRate', …) requests one: increases apply immediately, while reductions or prices for unknown usage remain pending and return 0 changed costs. This read shows effective rates only; review pending model/date/exact prices in the affected agent's or routine's Spend cap block. Only that native Accept can apply them; pages and MCP cannot approve.
routines_runs_and_machines.role: Everything the Routines tab, run detail, run evidence, Worktrees panel and Machines panel show. Every call returns the same shape as its MCP twin (named in brackets): a dashboard and an agent see the same data. Reads only: nothing runs, nothing is marked. Times inside routine rows are RFC 3339 strings; *AtMs / *At numbers are epoch milliseconds.
routines_runs_and_machines.routine: await codesense.routine({key}) [routine_get data] → {id, scope, owner, owner_name, armed_here, runs_on, enabled, revision, schedule_in_words, routine (the full definition: name, task, trigger, agent, policy, ...), runs: [this Mac's last 5 runs]}. Rejects `validation: …` for an unknown key.
routines_runs_and_machines.routine_run: await codesense.routineRun({runId}) [routine_run data] → one routineRuns() row plus {routine_id, routine_name}.
routines_runs_and_machines.routine_runs: await codesense.routineRuns({key, limit?, before?}) [routine_runs data] → {runs: [{run_id, revision, source, phase, reason, linked_run_id, created_at, started_at, ended_at, result_text, detail, agent}], next_before}. Newest first; limit default 50, max 200; pass next_before as before for the next page (null on the last). phase: queued | running | succeeded | failed | needs_you (result_text is its question) | ended (exited without signal_done) | timed_out | cancelled | skipped (reason says why) | coalesced (folded into linked_run_id). result_text: what the agent produced (its signal_done summary); detail: why the run ended (a launch refusal, an unfilled task, a signal-only CLI's exit summary), or null; wake, machine and admission runs still explain themselves in result_text.
routines_runs_and_machines.routines: await codesense.routines() [routine_list data] → [{id, scope (personal|team), org, team, name, schedule_in_words, agent, where, runs_on (one_mac|each_mac), enabled (this Mac's switch), next_run_at, last_run: {status, reason?, at}|null, owner, owner_name, created_by, armed_here, needs_you, revision}]. `id` is the key every other routine call takes.
routines_runs_and_machines.run: await codesense.run({runId, maxArtifactBytes?}) [read_run] → {outcome (a runs() row, or null), transcript: {turns: [{role (assistant|user|result), text?, tool_calls?: [{name, input?, result?, is_error?}], usage?: {input_tokens?, output_tokens?}}]} | null, artifact (the tail of its captured output, secrets redacted, or null), artifactTruncated}. maxArtifactBytes default 65536, max 1048576. Render transcript text and artifact with textContent.
routines_runs_and_machines.run_evidence: await codesense.runEvidence({runId, storyId?}) [read_run_evidence] → null (still running, no outcome recorded, or no story) | {header: {runId, storyId, automationId?, trigger: {kind: 'attributed', source} | {kind: 'preEnvelope'} (no trigger recorded), scheduledAt?, firedAt?, startedAt?, endedAt?, status? (success|failed|needs-attention), summary? (secrets redacted), workflowRevisionId?}, run: {runId, parentRunId?, originNodeId?, correlationId, steps: [{stepExecutionId, nodeId, attempts: [{attemptId, attemptOrdinal (1-based), runId (pass to run() for that attempt's transcript and output), result (passed|failed|pending)}]}]}, perNodeResults: [{nodeId, summary?, outputs?: [{key, value (any JSON)}], artifacts?: [{kind (file|pr|entity), reference, label?}], footprint?: [{kind, reference, change (created|modified)}]}], authority (durable|currentStoreFallback; same shape either way)}. storyId defaults to the story the run's outcome names; pass it only for a run that worked several stories. Times are RFC 3339; absent lists are empty. Everything the built-in run-evidence view draws.
routines_runs_and_machines.run_work_product: await codesense.runWorkProduct({runId}) [read_run_work_product] → {branch} (the git branch the run produced) | null. The repository is the runs() row's outcome.work_product.source_repo ({owner, repo}).
routines_runs_and_machines.runs: await codesense.runs({limit?}) [list_runs] → [{outcome: {story_id, run_id, status (success|failed|needs-attention), summary?, exit_code?, started_at?, ended_at, source (signal|process_exit), automation_id?, trigger_source?, workspace?}, validated (completed|needs-attention|failed: the state to show), has_structured_transcript}] — the latest outcome of every agent run on this Mac, newest first (limit default 50, max 500). A run still going is not listed: sessions() shows it.
routines_runs_and_machines.session_read: await codesense.sessionRead({sessionId, include?: [conversation] or [turns], cursor?, limit?, turn?, toolUseId?}) [session_read] → joined session record, nativeSessionIds, models/cost (reported|rate_table|mixed|null), tools allowed/used (usedState and usedReason; used is null when absent/unsupported/unavailable, retained on expiry; firstError is the earliest indexed failure, firstRetainedError is the first outside droppedTurns or null, each with turn/toolUseId for a verified lookup), story, run, tasks, timing and unavailable reasons. retries is null (no recorded retry signal). Unknown cost is null with a reason. Conversation include returns the existing page and explicit availability state. Turns include returns the same page as summaries {index, role, tsMs, text (200 chars), toolCalls, toolErrors, model} with no tool input or result text, and the answer holds only session {sessionId, cli, branch, timing}, story and turns (not both includes); the app only, not published. Runtime reads are machine-wide; caller scope only gates story enrichment.
routines_runs_and_machines.session_usage: await codesense.sessionUsage({sinceMs?, untilMs?, sessionId?, cwd?, story?, limit?, cursor?}) [session_usage] → {sessions, days, totals, total, nextCursor?}: nextCursor is present only when more sessions follow (pass it back as cursor, with the same other args, to read the next page; total, totals and days count the current matches on every page; during a walk a session that becomes active moves to the first page; a walk is complete when its distinct sessionIds equal total, otherwise walk again from page 1 through continuation, merging by sessionId, up to 2 recovery rewalks; after that report the truthful latest N of M.); per session cli (claude, codex or opencode), tokens {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, messages, models, firstAtMs, lastAtMs, org, team and agent (null when unattributed), machineId (the machine it ran on, as machines() names it: 'local' for this Mac), story {id, title, status, epic, basis?} (the story the session was spent on: its story worktree, else the story its launch was opened for, else a context worktree named <team>/<epic>-<n> with basis 'associated' (no basis means exact); null when not tied to one; story: 'DEMO-5' keeps only that story's sessions), costUsd (null when a model has no list price on file), unpricedModels; days: per local day totals. Covers this Mac and the remote machines it connects to. Each model call counts once, including Codex's start-up cache warm-up, which Codex's own total leaves out.
routines_runs_and_machines.setup: await codesense.setup() [describe_setup] → {attribution}: whether line attribution and turn-link capture work on this Mac, the same object describe_setup returns under attribution. A passive read: it never installs, launches or refreshes. attribution: status {kind: active (git-ai installed, supported and its daemon answers; a repo's own setting can still keep a worktree off, shown on worktrees rows) | not_installed | installing | install_failed with message | unsupported_version with found | unsupported with reason | error with message; off with a reason appears only if a state ever reports it here, per-launch states are on worktrees rows}, binary (path), gitAiVersion, daemonReachable, warnings [text], previousBinary (null | {version, replacement, path}: the last git-ai replacement receipt), supportedVersions, notesRef (sense: notes stay on this Mac), notesPushRepos (repos set to push notes), daemonRepoRoots (how many attached clones CodeSense lists in git-ai's daemon_repo_roots; 0: no list, every repo; null while none resolves and the earlier list is kept), capture {lastSweepAt (epoch ms, null until the first sweep since the app started), trigger (startup|watcher or null), clonesSwept, logsSeen, logsNew, traceRowsStored, sessionMappingRowsStored (counts of the last startup or watcher pass, since app start; zero when none has run), watchErrors (registration failures in the latest watch reconciliation), lastError (the latest unresolved fixed phase message, no paths)}. Published (shared) dashboards declare `live: {queries: [setup]}` and get an allow-list only: status {kind, reason? (present only when the status is off)}, gitAiVersion, daemonReachable, supportedVersions, notesRef, daemonRepoRoots (a count) and the whole capture block; never the binary path, warnings or status message text, nor the previousBinary receipt or notesPushRepos. Always this Mac's values. Example: `const {attribution:a}=await codesense.setup(); rows=[['status',a.status.kind],['git-ai',a.gitAiVersion??'none'],['daemon',a.daemonReachable],['last sweep',a.capture.lastSweepAt??'not yet since start'],['logs new',a.capture.logsNew],['last error',a.capture.lastError??'none']]`.
routines_runs_and_machines.story_changes: await codesense.storyChanges({storyId, only?}) [story_changes] → all linked sessions (sessionRead facts plus basis), tasks with review ids, totals {sessions,costUsd,wallMs,activeMs,idleMs,reviewRounds,reviewTasks,lines}, unavailable, historyAsOf, warnings. reviewRounds counts the story's complete phase:review review-rounds markers, never wave/use observations (null with unavailable.reviewRounds when unreadable); reviewTasks counts review tasks (else marker tasks, warnings.reviewTasks; null with unavailable.reviewTasks); warnings.reviewRounds says when they disagree. totals.lines {ai:{total,byRuntime:{<listed CLI id>:n,other:n+unlisted}},human,unattributed,total} counts the lines added by every landed non-merge commit of the story (an unmerged branch is unavailable.branches), whatever limit or cursor (ai: exact agent author in git-ai notes; human: exact human author; unattributed: no note, unknown or association only, never human); it is null with unavailable.lines when any commit cannot be attributed (no checkout, objects not local, notes changing, incomplete history), never partial. prs[] lists merged PRs found locally, so mergedAt (committer time of mergedSha, epoch ms) is always set. Unknown cost is null with a reason; wall spans sessions, active/idle sum them. Includes branches/worktrees, locally resolved PRs and commits, totals.commits/files, planned/plannedBase, actual file facts (lines:{added,removed}|null and linesReason) and plannedUntouched. File lines use a containing branch range once, or lines changed by this story’s merged PRs against each first parent once; incomparable branches keep file lines null with unavailable.fileLines. PR url/urlReason use only local origin metadata. Commits include author. limit (default100,max500) and cursor page commits; total is known, stale cursors refused. Missing branch/squash/open PR facts carry unavailable reasons, without network; only a trail missing its merge fetches origin once (10 s bound; unavailable.historyFetch). historyAsOf {fetchedAt, originHead}. Published query shares commit sha/date, repo-relative tracked file facts and PR/merged SHAs with link basis, worktree state/basis, session id/models/cost/timing and task ids/reviews; no host or worktree paths, records, accounts, branch names, commit subjects, goals or summaries. Private reads accept include:["ranges"] for current-page introduced added-line ranges with resolver session/native IDs, basis and reasons, plus rangesBasis/rangesReason; default/empty include omits these fields. No-note/merge/unavailable reads preserve durable facts with explicit reasons. The resolver still attributes the full file internally. Published queries reject include and exclude ranges. No conversation. only?: [tasks|sessions|commits|prs|branches|worktrees|actual|reviews] answers just those arrays with totals; tasks, sessions and reviews never read git, and without a git array totals.commits, files and lines are null (unavailable.commits, files and lines say why) and a cursor is stale. reviews = the story's complete review rounds {id,round,phase,scope,skill,subjectKind,subjectRef,subjectRev,high,medium,low,dismissed,converged,reportedAt}; published queries drop id, subjectKind and subjectRef.
routines_runs_and_machines.story_totals: await codesense.storyTotals({storyIds}) [story_totals] → {stories: {<id as asked>: {totals, unavailable: {field: index into reasons}, computedAtMs, refreshing?} | {pending: true} | {error}}, reasons, pending, indexing: {done, total}} for 1 to 500 ids in one answer, from the Mac's story totals index; it never walks git. kit.storyTotals(ids) and CS.storyTotals(ids) take any number of ids, ask in parts (500 in the app; hosted, as many as fit the hosted 2 KB args limit, about 120 to 150) and merge one answer, renumbering reasons, asking again for rest, with source cache and the oldest answered_at when any part came from the cache. totals equals storyChanges({storyId}).totals and unavailable its unavailable reasons. Each ready story also has mergedAt (the latest merge time of its merged PRs, epoch ms; null with mergedAtReason), prs (its newest 5 merged PRs as {number, merged}) with prsTotal, and runtimes (sorted ids of the CLIs that reported its sessions' usage), from the same computation. It also has firstActivityAt and lastActivityAt (epoch ms over the story's sessions' usage, commits, merges, tasks and review rounds; null with activityReason when none is recorded) and openSessions (sessions with observed timing and no end that were active in the 15 minutes before computedAtMs, by usage or turn); a row computed before these existed answers them null with activityReason refreshing while it is recomputed, never pending. linesInProgress is the lines on story branches not merged yet, shaped like totals.lines (null with linesInProgressReason); they move into totals.lines on merge (after a squash or rebase merge, lines stay here while the story's branch ref still exists, local or on origin, until it is deleted). While a story's commits are still being counted its lines are the earlier ones with refreshing true, or unavailable ("counting in the background") when it had none, never 0. pending: not indexed yet and queued; show Loading and ask again, never 0. refreshing: a commit, merge, session, task or review marker changed the story since computedAtMs and a recompute is queued. indexing counts the scope's indexed stories (done of total). An answer past 240 KB is cut: truncated: true and rest lists the ids to ask again. Published storyTotals pins storyIds like storyChanges.storyId (every id must pass), shares totals whole and only the reasons storyChanges publishes, and answers {error: failed}.
routines_runs_and_machines.why_line: await codesense.whyLine({repo, rev?, story?, path, start, end}) [why_line] → committed line attribution from the bound local checkout's history, without fetching. An omitted rev is the story's merged SHA, else its branch head, else origin's default branch, never the checkout's HEAD (revSource says which; historyAsOf {fetchedAt, originHead}); lines are 1-based inclusive, end - start <= 2000. Returns resolvedCommit, notesRef, ranges with exact/associated/unknown basis and live joined sessions. Linked exact agent turn pointers are {sessionId,toolUseId,turn,reason?}, with a zero-based index from stored conversation metadata. Missing mappings use range.unavailable.turn; expired or dropped text keeps its index with a reason. Startup sweeps retained completed archives and live logs for attached clones with attribution enabled; completed archive events also capture while the app is open; exact-range queries reconcile on demand for these commits and parents. Stored mappings survive log deletion. Logs pruned before either capture cannot be recovered; no retention interval is assumed. Published turn and unavailable values use nested allow-lists. Missing local objects return unavailable. Full in-app JSON matches MCP; published queries omit native session ids, records, accounts, host paths and conversation.
routines_runs_and_machines.worktrees: await codesense.worktrees() [list_worktrees] → {rows, reaped}: this Mac's managed worktrees. Each row: kind (story|epicIntegration|orphan), workspaceKey (story id, epic id or clone path to group by), path, branch, dirty, repoPath, liveCliSession; a story row adds storyId, sourceRepo, syncStatus, failureReason, storySourcePath, orgSlug, team, orphaned, lastReverseSyncAt, lastReverseSyncBy, attribution (null before any agent launch there; else {status, gitAiVersion, checkedAt}: what git-ai line-attribution capture was at the LAST launch, checkedAt in epoch ms; status.kind is active (hooks and env were wired, not proof a checkpoint was seen), off with reason disabled_for_repo | notes_would_push | not_managed_worktree | repo_not_attached (the worktree's repo isn't attached on this Mac; attach its clone to track the next launch), installing (relaunch after completion), install_failed with message, not_installed, unsupported_version with found, unsupported with reason (including platform or newer), or error with message); an epicIntegration row adds epicId, owner, repo.

sessions.live: const off = codesense.onSessions((list, err) => render(list)) — runs now and again whenever the roster changes; call off() to stop.
sessions.read: codesense.sessions() → the list_sessions rows: [{handle, displayName, state, launchedBy, unread, oldestUnreadAt, subagents?, story?, workspace?, machine?, role?, avatar?, agent?, progress?}]. subagents: how many of its agent's subagents run now (absent at none); state stays the agent's own, so one whose turn ended while they work is idle with subagents: N. progress: its latest signal_progress, {phase: planning|dev|review|pr|blocked|done, step?, total? (step of total), note?, atMs}, present once it reported one. state: running | idle (turn finished) | needs-you (awaiting permission) | exited | offline (its machine is disconnected; it may still run there) | unknown. unread: unread messages to its own handle (null when unreadable); oldestUnreadAt: RFC 3339. machine: 'This Mac' or the machine's label. agent: the saved Agent id it runs. role/avatar: display labels its launcher gave it.
sessions.stop: await codesense.act('stopSession', {handle}) stops any listed session.

sdk.summary: queryContext({…, select: ["summary", …]}) adds row.summary to each row: a story/bug/spike/epic's overview — the text of the first configured summary heading (Settings → Summary headings, default ## Purpose then ## Story; the same matcher as validate_story), as plain text (Markdown links, emphasis, code and bullets removed, HTML tags removed, entities decoded), whitespace collapsed, capped at 500 characters; null when no heading matches within the first 16 KB of the file, or for other files. Feature-detect it: an older CodeSense omits the key (`'summary' in row`). Parsed once when the index reads the file, so selecting it costs no file reads. Rows carry it only when selected.

theme.live: const off = codesense.onTheme((theme) => …) — runs now (once known) and on every theme change.
theme.read: await codesense.theme() → {scheme: 'dark'|'light', tokens: {'--cs-bg': '#282a36', …}}, resolving once the host has sent it.
theme.tokens: The host sets the app's theme on the page root as CSS custom properties, in a right pane, a centre tab and an inbox message alike: --cs-bg (the surface the page sits on), --cs-fg, --cs-muted-fg, --cs-border, --cs-surface (a raised card), --cs-accent, --cs-accent-fg, --cs-link, --cs-danger, --cs-success, --cs-warning, --cs-font-sans, plus --cs-color-scheme (dark|light). Style with var(--cs-fg) etc. and paint the body with var(--cs-bg) (or use the kit's `cs-app` body class). In a pane, and in a centre tab when the page uses --cs-* tokens, the root's `color-scheme` is set to match too. Do NOT use prefers-color-scheme: the surface follows the viewer theme, which can be dark while the app is light.
